418.content: Many human cultures live skin-to-skin with virtually everyone, maintaining continuous physical contact as the primary mode of social interaction. Modern Western cultures are historically unusual in the degree of touch avoidance and personal-space norms. The reduction of casual physical contact in WEIRD societies represents a mismatch with the ancestral pattern of continuous tactile social regulation.

419.quote: The key to understanding how humans evolved and why we are so different from other animals is to recognize that we are a cultural species. Probably over a million years ago, members of our evolutionary lineage began learning from each other in such a way that culture became cumulative.
419.content: Humans are a cultural species. Over a million years ago, members of our evolutionary lineage began learning from each other so that culture became cumulative. Tool-making skills, tracking know-how, and edible-plant knowledge improved and aggregated across generations until the toolkit became so complex that individuals could not figure it out on their own over a lifetime. Culture became the species' primary adaptation.

420.quote: cultural evolution initiated a process of self-domestication, driving genetic evolution to make us prosocial, docile, rule followers who expect a world governed by social norms monitored and enforced by communities.
420.content: Cultural evolution initiated a process of self-domestication, driving genetic evolution to make humans prosocial, docile, rule-following organisms who expect a world governed by social norms monitored and enforced by communities. Cultural products like fire, cooking, tools, clothing, and language became the main selective pressures that genetically shaped human minds and bodies - culture-gene coevolution creating a new kind of animal.

421.quote: One lone woman equipped with only the cumulative know-how of her ancestors survived for eighteen years whereas fully provisioned and well-financed teams of experienced explorers struggled in Australia, Texas, and the Arctic.
421.content: Without culturally transmitted knowledge about how to locate and process plants, fashion tools, and avoid dangers, humans do not last long as hunter-gatherers. European explorers who became separated from their cultural knowledge base routinely perished despite access to the same environments that sustained indigenous populations for millennia. One lone woman equipped with ancestral cumulative know-how survived eighteen years where provisioned, financed exploration teams failed.

422.quote: I remain convinced that it is useful, at least in the present state of our knowledge, to 'dissect' the master question into three stages.
422.content: Tinbergen's four questions framework: the complete study of behavior requires investigating (1) causation (mechanism - what internal and external stimuli trigger the behavior), (2) ontogeny (development - how the behavior develops during the organism's lifetime), (3) survival value (function - what adaptive advantage the behavior confers), and (4) evolution (phylogeny - how the behavior evolved across species). These four levels of analysis are complementary, not competing.

423.quote: It is a striking fact that displacement activities often occur in a situation in which the fighting drive and the drive to escape are both activated.
423.content: Displacement activities occur when two incompatible drives are simultaneously activated - for example, when fighting drive and escape drive conflict at a territory boundary, animals perform apparently irrelevant behaviors like preening or feeding. These activities reveal the competing motivational programs underlying behavior and demonstrate that behavior is not a simple stimulus-response chain but emerges from the interaction of multiple motivational systems.

424.quote: Oystercatcher incubating 'supernormal' clutch of five eggs in preference to natural clutch of three.
424.content: Supernormal stimuli: animals preferentially respond to exaggerated versions of natural sign stimuli. Oystercatchers incubate giant artificial eggs over their own normal-sized clutch. Herring gull chicks peck more vigorously at a red knitting needle with white stripes than at a realistic model of the parent's bill. The innate releasing mechanism responds to specific stimulus features, and artificial exaggeration of those features produces stronger responses than the natural stimulus.

425.quote: A wave of obesity and chronic, preventable illnesses and disabilities is sweeping across the globe. These preventable diseases include certain cancers, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, heart disease, strokes, kidney disease, some allergies, dementia, depression, anxiety, insomnia, and other illnesses.
425.content: A wave of preventable chronic illnesses is sweeping across the globe: certain cancers, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, heart disease, strokes, kidney disease, allergies, dementia, depression, anxiety, insomnia. Billions also suffer from lower back pain, fallen arches, plantar fasciitis, myopia, arthritis, constipation, and acid reflux. These are mismatch diseases - conditions whose prevalence surged when human environments departed from the conditions under which human bodies evolved.

426.quote: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammation of the arterial walls that results from how you shuttle cholesterol and triglycerides (fats) around your body.
426.content: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammation of the arterial walls resulting from how the body shuttles cholesterol and triglycerides. The process is driven by the mismatch between ancestral diet/activity patterns (which kept LDL cholesterol low and HDL high) and modern sedentary high-calorie environments that invert this ratio. Chronic arterial inflammation is a paradigm case of allostatic load from metabolic mismatch.

427.quote: Walk or run 10 kilometers (6.2 miles) a day (barefoot, of course), climb a few trees, chase squirrels in the park, throw rocks, eschew chairs, and sleep on a board instead of a mattress.
427.content: Modern sedentary lifestyle is directly mismatched with ancestral activity patterns. Walking or running 10+ kilometers daily, climbing trees, throwing, eschewing chairs, and sleeping on hard surfaces were normal for most of human evolutionary history. The primal-lifestyle movement correctly identifies the mismatch but often oversimplifies the solution. The key insight is that the chair-based, shoe-bound, indoor modern lifestyle is a novel environment that human bodies are poorly adapted to navigate.

428.quote: I examine the physiological and biochemical effects of touch and massage therapy, including decreased heart rate, blood pressure, and cortisol and increased oxytocin.
428.content: Touch and massage therapy produce measurable neurobiological effects: decreased heart rate, blood pressure, and cortisol; increased oxytocin. Brain imaging shows activation of orbitofrontal cortex and caudate cortex during affective touch. The physiological pathway involves stimulation of pressure receptors leading to vagal activation, which in turn modulates the HPA axis and immune function.

429.quote: Women with physical contact before stress exhibited significantly lower cortisol and heart rate responses to stress but no different plasma oxytocin levels.
429.content: Physical contact from a partner before stress significantly lowers cortisol and heart rate responses. A ten-minute neck and shoulder massage produced greater stress buffering than verbal social support or no partner interaction. Touch-based social regulation operates through direct physiological pathways (cortisol suppression, cardiovascular calming) not just psychological comfort.

430.quote: We compared 'grandparent' volunteers massaging infants (figure 2.2), with 'grandparent' volunteers being massaged themselves. Both experiences had positive effects, including such lifestyle changes as participants having more social contacts, drinking less coffee, and making fewer trips to the doctor's office.
430.content: Elderly volunteers who massaged infants showed positive health effects: more social contacts, less coffee consumption, fewer doctor visits. Being massaged and giving massage both produced benefits. This reciprocal caregiving-through-touch model demonstrates that touch regulation is bidirectional - the giver of touch benefits physiologically as well as the receiver.

431.quote: Religious rituals that galvanize greater prosociality.
431.content: Religious rituals galvanize greater prosociality and bind groups through synchronized behavior. Cultural evolution shaped ritual practices that create collective identity, coordinate group action, and suppress free-riding. Rituals are not arbitrary cultural decorations but functional mechanisms for maintaining cooperation at scales beyond face-to-face reciprocity.

432.quote: The secret of our species' success resides not in the power of our individual minds, but in the collective brains of our communities.
432.content: The secret of our species' success resides not in the power of individual minds but in the collective brains of communities. Humans became simultaneously the most cooperative and the most warlike of primates - large-scale societies enabling both technological innovation and intergroup conflict. The collective brain hypothesis explains why larger, more interconnected populations innovate faster.

433.quote: The innate releasing mechanism usually seems to correspond more or less with the properties of the environmental object or situation at which the reaction is normally directed.
433.content: The innate releasing mechanism corresponds to specific properties of environmental stimuli - sign stimuli. Animals respond to specific stimulus features (color, shape, movement pattern) rather than to the whole object. When artificial stimuli exaggerate these features beyond natural ranges, they produce supernormal responses - animals prefer the artificial exaggeration to the real thing. This demonstrates that the releasing mechanism is an open loop: it responds to features, not to the object as a whole.

434.quote: These 'explosions' or 'vacuum activities' in a captive starling. It performed repeatedly the whole behaviour pattern of insect hunting, from watching the prey through catching, killing, and swallowing, without any discernible external stimulus.
434.content: Vacuum activities: a captive starling performed the entire behavior pattern of insect hunting - watching, catching, killing, and swallowing - without any discernible external stimulus. Lorenz confirmed no insects were present. This demonstrates that motivational energy accumulates internally and can discharge behavior without any environmental trigger, when the threshold has been lowered sufficiently by deprivation.

435.quote: Routinely sleeping less than six or seven hours a night demolishes your immune system, more than doubling your risk of cancer.
435.content: Routinely sleeping less than six or seven hours a night demolishes the immune system, more than doubling cancer risk. Insufficient sleep is a key lifestyle factor determining whether you will develop Alzheimer's disease. Sleep disruption contributes to cardiovascular disease, stroke, depression, anxiety, and suicidality. No aspect of human health is spared by sleep loss.

436.quote: Central to many of the questions in the opening paragraph is the powerful sculpting force of your twenty-four-hour rhythm, also known as your circadian rhythm.
436.content: The circadian rhythm - the twenty-four-hour biological pacemaker - orchestrates immune function, metabolic timing, hormonal release, body temperature, and cognitive performance. The suprachiasmatic nucleus generates this rhythm and is synchronized by light-dark cycles. Artificial lighting, screens, and shift work disrupt this synchronization, producing circadian misalignment that cascades through every physiological system.

437.quote: it is during sleep that this neural sanitization work kicks into high gear. Associated with the pulsing rhythm of deep NREM sleep comes a ten- to twentyfold increase in effluent expulsion from the brain.
437.content: During deep NREM sleep, the glymphatic system - the brain's metabolic waste clearance mechanism - kicks into high gear. A ten- to twentyfold increase in cerebrospinal fluid flushing occurs during NREM sleep, clearing amyloid-beta and tau proteins associated with Alzheimer's pathology. Without adequate deep sleep, this neural detoxification cannot occur, and the toxic waste accumulates.

438.quote: Sleep deprived people are perceived as less attractive, less healthy, and more tired compared with when they are well rested.
438.content: Sleep deprivation is visible in the phenotype: independent judges rate sleep-deprived individuals as less healthy, less attractive, and more fatigued than well-rested individuals from photographs alone. On Cor's reading (not something the study tested, since it measured only perceived health and attractiveness), this makes sleep a phenotypic fitness signal: the physiological state produced by adequate sleep is visible to potential mates and social partners, and sleep loss degrades that signal.

439.quote: To plot what industry insiders call the 'bliss point,' or the precise amount of sugar or fat or salt that will send consumers over the moon. At a laboratory in White Plains, New York, industry scientists who perform this alchemy walked me, step by step, through the process of engineering a new soda so that I could see the creation of bliss firsthand.
439.content: The food industry engineers bliss points - the precise amount of sugar, fat, or salt that sends consumers over the moon. Industry scientists mathematically optimize the hedonic response curve for each product, finding the exact concentration that maximizes craving. This is not accidental food design but systematic exploitation of the reward system's response to ancestrally rare nutrient signals.

440.quote: These were the three pillars of processed food, the creators of crave, and each of the CEOs needed them in huge quantities to turn their products into hits.
440.content: Salt, sugar, and fat are the three pillars of processed food - the creators of crave. Each CEO needed them in huge quantities to turn products into hits. Officials discussed the power of foods to create cravings that overwhelm the best intentions of dieters. Industry-wide limits on mainline products (not just niche diet items) would be needed to diminish these cravings, but competitive pressure prevents any single company from unilaterally reducing palatability.

441.quote: The mechanism of learned helplessness is now very well-charted biologically, and the original theory got it backward. Passivity in response to shock is not learned. It is the default, unlearned response to prolonged aversive events and it is mediated by the serotonergic activity of the dorsal raphe nucleus, which in turn inhibits escape.
441.content: The mechanism of learned helplessness has been biologically well-charted and the original theory got it backward. Passivity in response to prolonged aversive events is not learned - it is the default, unlearned response mediated by serotonergic activity of the dorsal raphe nucleus, which inhibits escape. What is actually learned is the detection of control: the prelimbic region of medial prefrontal cortex detects response-outcome contingency and inhibits the dorsal raphe, enabling active coping.

442.quote: Learned helplessness in the laboratory - combining the animal and human experimental results - produced eight of the nine symptoms [of depression], with the only exception being suicide and suicidal thoughts.
442.content: Learned helplessness in the laboratory produces eight of the nine DSM symptoms of depression (excepting suicidal thoughts). The prelimbic medial prefrontal cortex detects contingency between behavior and outcomes and inhibits the dorsal raphe nucleus, restoring the capacity for active escape. When this detection circuit fails - due to chronic uncontrollable stress, developmental adversity, or prefrontal damage - the default passivity state persists as clinical depression.

443.quote: SBT suggests the human brain expects access to social relationships that mitigate risk and diminish the level of effort needed to meet a variety of goals.
443.content: Social Baseline Theory: the human brain expects access to social relationships that mitigate risk and diminish the level of effort needed to meet goals. Social and metabolic resources are treated almost interchangeably by the brain - isolation is processed as resource scarcity. Violations of the social proximity expectation increase cognitive and physiological effort as the brain perceives fewer available resources.

444.quote: Although the brain is highly responsive to perceived threat, even simple handholding can substantially attenuate threat responses.
444.content: SBT describes two mechanisms for social regulation: risk distribution (safety in numbers) and load sharing (distribution of effort toward shared goals). During supportive handholding, the threat-responsive brain returns to a baseline state of relative calm - not through activation of regulatory circuitry but through decreased perceived demand. The brain encodes relational partners as extensions of the self, effectively pooling bioenergetic resources.

445.quote: Disgust is an evolved psychological system for protecting organisms from infection through disease avoidant behaviour. This 'behavioural immune system', present in a diverse array of species, exhibits universal features that orchestrate hygienic behaviour in response to cues of risk of contact with pathogens.
445.content: Disgust is an evolved psychological system for protecting organisms from infection through disease-avoidant behavior. This behavioral immune system is present in diverse species and exhibits universal features that orchestrate hygienic behavior in response to cues of pathogen contact risk. Three specialized learning mechanisms modify the disgust response: the Garcia effect (one-trial aversion learning), evaluative conditioning, and the law of contagion.

446.quote: Contact with disgust elicitors, real or imagined, is associated with (i) a characteristic facial expression... (ii) behaviour patterns that include withdrawal, distancing, stopping or dropping the object of disgust... (iii) physiological changes including lowered blood pressure and galvanic skin response.
446.content: Disgust elicitors are universal across cultures: bodily wastes, body contents, sick/deformed/dead/unhygienic people. Contact with disgust elicitors produces a characteristic facial expression, withdrawal/distancing behaviors, and physiological changes including lowered blood pressure and galvanic skin response. Brain imaging reveals a specific neural disgust network including anterior insular cortex, basal ganglia, and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex. All societies demonstrate individual and group-level hygiene behaviors.

447.quote: To keep playing - to stay in that machine zone where nothing else matters. It's like being in the eye of a storm, is how I'd describe it. Your vision is clear on the machine in front of you but the whole world is spinning around you, and you can't really hear anything.
447.content: Machine gambling produces a 'zone' state - an absorptive dissociation where nothing else matters. Gamblers describe it as being 'in the eye of a storm' where vision narrows to the machine, the world spins around you, and you cannot hear anything. The primary reinforcer is not winning money but staying in the zone. The gambling industry explicitly designs for 'time-on-device' (TOD) as the target metric.

448.quote: Modern slot machines are rarely the work of one company; they are symphonies of individual technologies that come together to create a single experience.
448.content: Modern slot machines are engineered systems assembled from 1,200+ individual parts by teams of up to 300 people including mathematicians, graphic artists, marketers, and software engineers. They employ 'losses disguised as wins' (LDWs) - multiline outcomes where the total return is less than the wager but the machine celebrates with lights and sounds, producing the reinforcing arousal of a win on what is actually a net loss. Near-miss effects are engineered through clustering techniques that distort loss perception.

449.quote: that elusive point of absorption, beyond contingency
449.content: The zone state is described as absorption 'beyond contingency' - a narrowly focused attention state where control dissolves into automaticity. Machine gamblers seek the zone not to win but to escape - from anxiety, grief, boredom, social pain. The machine provides a predictable, controllable micro-environment that the rest of life cannot match. This is proxy hijacking of M6 (controllability) as much as M2 (pursuit).

450.content: The gambling industry designs for 'extinction' - continued play until total asset depletion. Variable-ratio reward schedules maintain play because the next reward could come at any time. The mathematical structure of the game is invisible to the player, who experiences only the surface (lights, sounds, near-misses) while the underlying probability structure ensures net loss over time. The house edge is designed to be imperceptible on a per-spin basis.

451.quote: dopamine's contribution appears to be chiefly to cause 'wanting' for hedonic rewards, more than 'liking' or learning for those rewards.
451.content: Dopamine's contribution to reward is chiefly to cause 'wanting' for hedonic rewards, more than 'liking' or learning. The wanting-liking dissociation means that dopamine attributes incentive salience to reward-related stimuli - making them attention-grabbing, attractive, and sought after - without necessarily making them pleasurable. This dissociation explains why addicts compulsively seek drugs they no longer enjoy.
451.where: Abstract and Introduction (source lines 20-32); sourced from Berridge 2007 Debate paper on disk

452.content: Hedonic 'liking' reactions are mediated by opioid systems in nucleus accumbens and ventral pallidum, not by dopamine. Dopamine codes incentive salience (wanting), not hedonic impact (liking). The hedonic reactions are homologous across mammals - humans share reaction details with hominids, moderately with monkeys, and lightly with rodents. This cross-species conservation of the liking system demonstrates its phylogenetic depth.
452.where: Section on Liking (source lines 183-242); sourced from Berridge 2007 Debate paper on disk

453.quote: We found a graded relationship between the number of categories of childhood exposure and each of the adult health risk behaviors and diseases that were studied.
453.content: The ACE Study (9,508 respondents) demonstrated a graded dose-response relationship between categories of childhood adversity (psychological abuse, physical abuse, sexual abuse, violence against mother, household substance abuse, mental illness, incarceration) and adult health outcomes. Persons with 4+ ACE categories had 4-12 fold increased risk for alcoholism, drug abuse, depression, and suicide attempts; 2-4 fold increased risk for smoking, poor health, STDs; 1.4-1.6 fold for inactivity and obesity. More than half of respondents reported at least one category. Adult diseases linked included ischemic heart disease, cancer, chronic lung disease, skeletal fractures, and liver disease.

454.quote: More than half of respondents reported at least one, and one-fourth reported two or more categories of childhood exposures.
454.content: The ACE dose-response gradient shows that childhood adversity is not a binary (traumatized/not) but a cumulative load: each additional category of exposure incrementally increases adult disease risk across behavioral, mental, and physical health domains. The clustering of risk behaviors (smoking, substance use, obesity, sexual risk-taking) suggests that these are not independent choices but downstream consequences of the same developmental calibration toward defensive/avoidant coping strategies.

455.quote: an epigenomic state of a gene can be established through behavioral programming, and it is potentially reversible.
455.content: Maternal licking/grooming and arched-back nursing in rats alters offspring epigenome at the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) gene promoter in the hippocampus via DNA methylation and histone acetylation changes. Offspring of high-LG mothers have lower glucocorticoid levels, less anxiety, better learning, and delayed brain aging. Methylation differences emerged over the first week of life, were reversed with cross-fostering, and persisted into adulthood. Central infusion of a histone deacetylase inhibitor removed group differences - demonstrating that an epigenomic state established through behavioral programming is potentially reversible.

456.quote: Offspring of mothers that showed high levels of LG and ABN were found to have differences in DNA methylation, as compared to offspring of low-LG-ABN mothers.
456.content: The specific epigenetic mechanism involves altered methylation at the NGFI-A transcription factor binding site in the GR promoter, changing GR expression in the hippocampus. This alters the negative feedback sensitivity of the HPA axis - high-LG offspring have more hippocampal GR, stronger negative feedback, and lower baseline glucocorticoid levels. The effect cascades: lower baseline stress hormones → less anxiety → better learning → delayed brain aging.

457.quote: our perceptions of space-time and objects have been shaped by natural selection to hide the truth and guide adaptive behaviors.
457.content: Interface Theory of Perception: through evolutionary game theory and genetic algorithms, veridical (truth-tracking) perceptions are routinely dominated by nonveridical strategies tuned to fitness. Our perceptions of space-time and objects have been shaped by natural selection to hide the truth and guide adaptive behaviors. An interface serves to guide useful actions, not to resemble truth. Veridical perceptions escape extinction only if fitness varies monotonically with truth.

458.quote: the FBT Theorem shows that the claim is false - that natural selection does not favor veridical perception.
458.content: The Fitness-Beats-Truth (FBT) Theorem: formal proof using evolutionary game theory and Bayesian decision theory that a strategy maximizing fitness payoff consistently outperforms a strategy attempting to estimate true world states. The fitness-only strategy dominates the truth strategy with this dominance increasing as the perceptual space expands. Natural selection does not favor veridical perception - the standard assumption is provably false.

459.quote: psychological mechanisms are designed to be predictably biased when the costs of false-positive and false-negative errors were asymmetrical over evolutionary history.
459.content: Error Management Theory (EMT): psychological mechanisms are designed to be predictably biased when the costs of false-positive and false-negative errors were asymmetrical over evolutionary history. Men's sexual overperception bias (overestimating women's sexual interest) and women's commitment underperception bias (underestimating men's commitment) are adaptive biases shaped by asymmetric error costs. EMT offers a systematic framework for predicting cognitive biases from ancestral cost asymmetries.

460.quote: Human cooperation is an evolutionary puzzle. Unlike other creatures, people frequently cooperate with genetically unrelated strangers, often in large groups, with people they will never meet again, and when reputation gains are small or absent.
460.content: Altruistic punishment: individuals punish defectors at personal cost with no material gain. Cooperation flourishes when altruistic punishment is possible and breaks down when it is ruled out. Negative emotions toward defectors are the proximate mechanism behind altruistic punishment. Human cooperation with unrelated strangers in large groups cannot be explained by kin selection, signaling theory, or reciprocal altruism alone - altruistic punishment is a key additional mechanism.

461.quote: the cost of chronic exposure to fluctuating or heightened neural or neuroendocrine response resulting from repeated or chronic environmental challenge.
461.content: Allostatic load is the cost of chronic exposure to fluctuating or heightened neural or neuroendocrine response resulting from repeated or chronic environmental challenge. Rather than maintaining constant internal conditions (homeostasis), physiologic systems fluctuate to meet demands from external forces - a state termed allostasis. The hidden cost of chronic stress accumulates over long time periods, acting as a predisposing factor for the effects of acute stressful life events.

462.quote: the hidden cost of chronic stress to the body over long time periods, which act as a predisposing factor for the effects of acute, stressful life events.
462.content: Individual susceptibility to allostatic load is shaped by behavioral responses coupled to physiologic and pathophysiologic changes beginning early in life. The allostasis framework replaces the static homeostasis model with a dynamic model where the body actively adjusts to anticipated demands - but this adjustment has a cumulative cost when chronically activated. The predisposing-factor model explains why the same acute stressor produces different health outcomes in different individuals.

463.quote: individuals with adequate social relationships have a 50% greater likelihood of survival compared to those with poor or insufficient social relationships.
463.content: Meta-analysis of 148 studies (308,849 participants, 7.5 year average follow-up): individuals with stronger social relationships had a 50% greater likelihood of survival (OR=1.50, 95% CI 1.42-1.59). This effect is comparable to smoking cessation and exceeds the influence of obesity and physical inactivity on mortality. Complex social integration measures showed the strongest effect (OR=1.91). The association held across age, sex, initial health status, cause of death, follow-up period, and geographic region.
463.where: PLoS Medicine, DOI: 10.1371/journal.pmed.1000316, PMID: 20668659 (open access full text)

464.quote: The overall effect was not moderated by participant sex, length of follow-up, initial health status of participants, or cause of death.
464.content: Social relationships predict mortality regardless of age, sex, initial health status, cause of death, or geographic region. The effect is not mediated by any single health behavior - it operates across all-cause mortality. Living alone (binary measure) shows the weakest effect (OR=1.19) while complex social integration measures show the strongest (OR=1.91), suggesting that relationship quality and network structure matter more than simple social contact.

465.quote: Species following the model should tend to evolve behaviour such that each organism appears to be attempting to maximize its inclusive fitness.
465.content: Hamilton's genetical mathematical model allows for interactions between relatives on one another's fitness. Using Wright's Coefficient of Relationship as the measure of replica genes in a relative, Hamilton found inclusive fitness - a quantity incorporating the maximizing property of Darwinian fitness. Species following the model tend to evolve behaviour where each organism appears to maximize its inclusive fitness, implying limited restraint on selfish competitive behaviour and possibility of limited self-sacrifices.

466.quote: To express the matter more vividly, in the world of our model organisms, whose behaviour is determined strictly by genotype, we expect to find that no one is prepared to sacrifice his life for any single person but that everyone will sacrifice it when he can thereby save more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins . . .
466.content: Hamilton's rule, in its modern canonical form, states that a social behaviour is favoured by natural selection when rB > C, where r is the coefficient of relatedness between actor and recipient, B is the fitness benefit to the recipient, and C is the fitness cost to the actor. Hamilton's original 1964 paper introduced this principle using a gain-ratio inequality (his condition for an altruistic action to be favoured was -k > 1/r, with k the ratio of gain and r Wright's coefficient of relationship); the compact "rB > C" algebraic notation is a later popularization. The principle explains when organisms will sacrifice personal fitness to benefit relatives and predicts that the altruism threshold decreases with increasing relatedness - in Hamilton's own example, an organism should sacrifice its life to save "more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins" (siblings r=0.5, cousins r=0.125).
466.where: Journal of Theoretical Biology 7(1):1-16 and 7(1):17-52, 1964. PMID: 5875341/5875340

467.quote: Human psychological mechanisms are adaptations that evolved to process environmental inputs, turning them into behavioral outputs that, on average, increase survival or reproductive prospects. Modern contexts, however, differ vastly from the environments that existed as human psychological mechanisms evolved.
467.content: Evolutionary mismatch occurs when human psychological mechanisms, adapted to process ancestral environmental inputs, encounter modern contexts that differ vastly from those environments. Many inputs now differ in quantity, intensity, or no longer have the same fitness associations, leading mechanisms to produce maladaptive output. Li et al. classify mismatch along four dimensions: source (natural vs human-induced), type (forced vs hijacked), cause (input changes vs output-consequence changes), and consequences (effects on reproductive fitness crossed with effects on individual well-being). Tables 1-3 provide worked examples for each dimension.
467.where: Current Directions in Psychological Science 27(1):38-44, 2018. DOI: 10.1177/0963721417731378

468.quote: Many inputs now differ in quantity and intensity or no longer have the same fitness associations, thereby leading many mechanisms to produce maladaptive output.
468.content: The mismatch framework has implications for public policy. Li et al. present specific examples: (1) despite modern sanitation benefits, immune systems evolved to be stimulated by bacterial exposure in infancy - overuse of antibacterial products may contribute to childhood asthma, allergies, and ear infections; (2) ecological conservation efforts have met limited success because conservation behavior is evolutionarily novel - humans evolved to consume local resources without concern when pollutant output was low and migration was feasible. Effective interventions should work with, rather than oppose, evolved tendencies such as self-interest, social status concerns, social imitation, and future discounting.
468.where: Current Directions in Psychological Science 27(1):38-44, 2018. DOI: 10.1177/0963721417731378

469.quote: The price of this accommodation to stress can be allostatic load, which is the wear and tear that results from chronic overactivity or underactivity of allostatic systems.
469.content: McEwen's 1998 NEJM review: the physiologic response to stress, allostatic load, reflects wear and tear from not only life experiences but also genetic load, individual lifestyle habits (diet, exercise, substance abuse), and developmental experiences. Hormones associated with stress protect the body short-term through allostasis but in the long run cause disease. Four conditions produce allostatic load: (1) repeated stressors, (2) lack of adaptation to repeated stressors, (3) prolonged response due to delayed shutdown, and (4) inadequate response leading to compensatory hyperactivity of other systems.

470.quote: Over 60 years ago, Selye recognized the paradox that the physiologic systems activated by stress can not only protect and restore but also damage the body.
470.content: Allostasis is the ability to achieve stability through change - the body's active adjustment to anticipated demands. Unlike homeostasis (maintaining constant internal conditions), allostasis recognizes that the body actively shifts its operating parameters in response to predicted demands. The cost of this active adjustment, when chronically required, is allostatic load. Selye recognized 60 years earlier that stress mediators can both protect and damage - McEwen's contribution is formalizing this paradox.

471.content: Eaton & Konner analyzed nutritional properties of wild game and uncultivated vegetable foods and evaluated archaeological remains to reconstruct Paleolithic diet composition. Their model was derived from 69 game and wild vegetable items. Humanity has existed as a genus for about 2 million years, with evolutionary history making definitive contributions to current genetic composition partly in response to dietary influences. The resulting evolutionary discordance between ancestral and modern diets is proposed as a major source of chronic disease.

472.content: The Paleolithic nutrition model identifies specific discordances between ancestral and modern diets: higher protein intake, lower carbohydrate (especially refined), much higher fiber, lower sodium, higher potassium, higher calcium from non-dairy sources, and substantially lower sugar consumption. The fat profile differs in kind, not just quantity - ancestral fats were predominantly unsaturated while modern diets are dominated by saturated and trans fats. These specific nutritional parameters define the mismatch that drives metabolic disease.

473.quote: More than half of respondents reported at least one, and one-fourth reported two or more categories of childhood exposures.
473.content: The ACE Study identified seven categories of childhood adversity and found that more than half of respondents reported at least one, and one-fourth reported two or more categories. The graded dose-response relationship - where each additional ACE category incrementally increases risk - demonstrates that childhood adversity is cumulative rather than categorical. Persons with 4+ categories had 4-12 fold increased health risk, suggesting a threshold effect where the cascade becomes self-reinforcing.

474.quote: methylation differences emerged over the first week of life, were reversed with cross-fostering, persisted into adulthood.
474.content: The cross-fostering experiment definitively proved that the epigenetic differences are caused by maternal behavior, not genetic inheritance. Pups born to low-LG mothers but raised by high-LG mothers developed the low-stress phenotype of their foster mothers, and vice versa. The pharmacological reversal via histone deacetylase inhibitor demonstrated that the epigenetic marks are modifiable even in adulthood, establishing that developmental calibration is potentially reversible - a finding with profound therapeutic implications.

475.quote: A model is presented to account for the natural selection of what is termed reciprocally altruistic behavior.
475.content: Trivers models the natural selection of reciprocally altruistic behavior and shows how selection operates against cheaters. The human psychological system that regulates reciprocal altruism explains friendship, dislike, moralistic aggression, gratitude, sympathy, trust, suspicion, trustworthiness, aspects of guilt, and forms of dishonesty and hypocrisy as adaptations to regulate the altruistic system.

476.quote: Three instances of altruistic behavior are discussed, the evolution of which the model can explain: (1) behavior involved in cleaning symbioses; (2) warning cries in birds: and (3) human reciprocal altruism.
476.content: Trivers presents three instances of reciprocal altruism: (1) cleaning symbioses between fish (cleaner wrasse and host grouper), where hosts refrain from eating cleaners despite opportunity; (2) warning cries in birds, reinterpreted as reciprocal altruism rather than kin selection; (3) human reciprocal altruism, the most complex form, regulated by an elaborate psychological system including friendship, moralistic aggression, gratitude, sympathy, trust, suspicion, and aspects of guilt.

477.quote: humans have innate needs to be seen as attractive to others. These needs form the basis for shame and mediate evaluations of social standing (status), social acceptance and social bonds.
477.content: Humans have innate needs to be seen as attractive to others, forming the basis for shame. Shame and humiliation derive from attacks on social attractiveness. Internal shame experience derives from submissive defense strategies signaling awareness of lost social standing to limit damage from higher-ranking individuals.

478.quote: For example, in shame the focus is on the self, while in humiliation the focus is on the harm done by others.
478.content: Shame, humiliation, and guilt differ as evolved social strategies: shame focuses on the self (submissive appeasement), humiliation focuses on harm done by others (agonistic challenge), guilt focuses on specific actions and consequences for others (relationship repair). These map onto different adaptive responses to different types of social evaluation threat.

479.content: Trivers identifies conditions maximizing the chance reciprocal altruism will be selected for: (1) many altruistic situations in the lifetime of the altruists, (2) a given altruist repeatedly interacts with the same small set of individuals, and (3) pairs of altruists are exposed symmetrically to altruistic situations - each able to render roughly equivalent benefits at roughly equivalent costs. He elaborates these into biological parameters: long lifetime, low dispersal rate, mutual dependence, parental care, dominance hierarchy structure (less dominance facilitates reciprocity), and aid in combat. Selection discriminates against cheaters when cheating has later adverse effects that outweigh the benefit of not reciprocating - the altruist curtails future altruistic gestures to the cheater.
479.where: Q Rev Biol 46(1):35-57, 1971. DOI: 10.1086/406755. Key conditions section.

480.quote: Regarding human reciprocal altruism, it is shown that the details of the psychological system that regulates this altruism can be explained by the model. Specifically, friendship, dislike, moralistic aggression, gratitude, sympathy, trust, suspicion, trustworthiness, aspects of guilt, and some forms of dishonesty and hypocrisy can be explained as important adaptations to regulate the altruistic system.
480.content: Gratitude, sympathy, trust, suspicion, and guilt are not arbitrary emotions but specific adaptations for regulating reciprocal altruism. Gratitude motivates reciprocation; sympathy motivates initial altruistic acts toward those in need; trust calibrates willingness to cooperate; suspicion monitors potential cheaters; guilt motivates relationship repair after defection. Each emotion functions as a regulatory mechanism within the reciprocal altruism system.
480.where: Q Rev Biol 46(1):35-57, 1971. DOI: 10.1086/406755. Human reciprocal altruism section.

481.quote: Shame and humiliation are associated with attacks on, and losses of, social attractiveness.
481.content: Social rank theory: humans evolved in social hierarchies where status determined access to resources and mates. Involuntary defeat strategy (IDS) is an evolved defensive response to status loss - when an organism loses rank and cannot escape, IDS produces behavioral inhibition, withdrawal, submissive signaling, and depressed mood. Depression in modern humans may reflect chronic activation of IDS in environments where status threats are persistent but escape or resolution is impossible.
481.where: Br J Med Psychol 70(2):113-147, 1997. PMID: 9210990. Social rank and IDS sections.

482.quote: The internal experiences of shame are derived from submissive strategies where one seeks to signal to others awareness of loss of social standing and limit possible damage.
482.content: Shame derives from an evolved submissive defense where the organism signals awareness of lost social standing to limit damage from higher-ranking individuals. The signal function of shame is appeasement: by displaying shame (gaze aversion, postural collapse, blushing), the organism communicates acceptance of lower rank and reduces the probability of continued attack. This is adaptive in hierarchical contexts but becomes pathological when chronically activated by modern status comparison (social media, workplace evaluation, academic competition).
482.where: Br J Med Psychol 70(2):113-147, 1997. PMID: 9210990. Shame mechanism section.

483.quote: Group size is found to be a function of relative neocortical volume, but the ecological variables are not. This is interpreted as evidence in favour of the social intellect theory and against the ecological theories.
483.content: Neocortex ratio (neocortex volume / rest-of-brain volume) predicts mean group size across 38 primate genera with r²=0.764 (t34=10.35, P<0.001). The regression equation log10(N) = 0.093 + 3.389·log10(CR) yields a predicted human group size of ~148, matching ethnographic data. Human neocortex ratio = 4.10.
483.where: Journal of Human Evolution 22(6):469-493, Table 1 and regression analysis

484.quote: even if it were true that energetic considerations constrain brain size, a proper functional explanation must still be given to explain why brains grow to the size they do.
484.content: Ecological variables fail to predict neocortex ratio. Percentage fruit in diet is unrelated. Range size and day journey length correlate in raw form but collapse to near zero when body mass is partialled out (residual r²=0.017 for range, r²<0.001 for day journey). Extractive foraging also fails once anthropoids are analyzed separately.
484.where: Journal of Human Evolution 22(6):469-493, ecological analysis section

485.quote: the number of neocortical neurons limits the organism's information-processing capacity and that this then limits the number of relationships that an individual can monitor simultaneously.
485.content: The number of neocortical neurons limits information-processing capacity, which constrains the number of relationships an individual can monitor simultaneously. The constraint operates on relationship structure and quality, not raw number of dyads.

486.quote: large groups are created by welding together sets of smaller grooming cliques
486.content: The regression slope of 3.389 (greater than 1) indicates large groups are created by combining smaller grooming cliques, not by uniformly expanding the social network. The cognitive limit lies in maintaining clique-internal relationship quality, not total relationship count.
486.where: Journal of Human Evolution 22(6):469-493, discussion of slope

487.quote: the data suggest that the information overload occurs in terms of the structure of relationships within tightly bonded grooming cliques rather than in terms of the total number of dyads within the group as a whole.
487.content: Female group size (r²=0.568) is a worse predictor of neocortex ratio than total group size (r²=0.764), indicating the cognitive constraint operates on total group membership, not just the reproductively relevant female core.
487.where: Journal of Human Evolution 22(6):469-493, female group size analysis

488.quote: Neocortex ratio is thus the single most powerful predictor of group size in these species.
488.content: Stepwise regression on 24 anthropoid primate species with 9 brain volume indices confirms neocortex ratio as the single most powerful predictor of group size. Independent contrasts analysis: r²=0.395, F(1,22)=15.39, P=0.001. No other brain index makes a significant contribution after neocortex ratio is included.
488.where: Evolutionary Anthropology 6(5):178-190, Table 2 and stepwise regression section. DOI: 10.1002/(SICI)1520-6505(1998)6:5<178::AID-EVAN5>3.0.CO;2-8

489.quote: brain evolution has not been a history of simple expansion in total volume. Rather, brain evolution has been mosaic in character, with both the rate and the extent of evolution having varied between components of the system.
489.content: Relative neocortex volume correlates with group size but NOT range area, while relative hippocampus size shows the reverse pattern (correlates with range but NOT group size). This double dissociation demonstrates that brain evolution is mosaic: specific brain components serve specific functions, not general intelligence.
489.where: Evolutionary Anthropology 6(5):178-190, hippocampus section, citing Barton & Purvis

490.quote: the various human groups that can be identified in any society seem to cluster rather tightly around a series of values (5, 12, 35, 150, 500, and 2,000) with virtually no overlap in the variance around these characteristic values.
490.content: Human social groups cluster at characteristic values of approximately 5, 12, 35, 150, 500, and 2,000 with virtually no overlap in variance between layers. These represent stable points in the degrees of familiarity and correspond to support clique, sympathy group, band, clan/village, mega-band, and tribe respectively.

491.quote: there is no intrinsic reason to suppose that memory per se is the issue. The social brain hypothesis is about the ability to manipulate information, not simply to remember it.
491.content: The social brain constraint is about ability to manipulate social information, not simply to remember individuals. Apes show grade-shifted cognitive demands per relationship compared to monkeys: apes are good psychologists (they read minds via theory of mind), while monkeys are good ethologists (they read behavior).
491.where: Evolutionary Anthropology 6(5):178-190, discussion of cognitive mechanisms

492.quote: Because of the structural complexity of postagricultural societies, I considered only traditional hunter-gatherer and small-scale horticultural societies. Although census data on such societies are limited, those that are available suggest that there is indeed a consistent group size in the region of 150 individuals (Fig. 7).
492.content: Ethnographic data from hunter-gatherer and horticultural societies validates the ~150 predicted by the primate neocortex regression (95% CI 100-230). The clan/village organizational level consistently clusters at this value, supporting the social brain hypothesis prediction for human-scale groups.

493.quote: In primates, there is a quantitative relationship between brain size and social group size (group size is a monotonic function of brain size)... In other mammals and birds, the relationship is a qualitative one: Large brains are associated with categorical differences in mating system.
493.content: The social brain hypothesis takes two distinct forms across taxa. In primates: a quantitative relationship where group size is a monotonic function of brain size. In all other mammals and birds: a qualitative relationship where pair-bonded species have categorically larger brains than non-pair-bonded species.
493.where: Annals of Human Biology 36(5):562-572, abstract and introduction. DOI: 10.1080/03014460902960289. PMID: 19575315

494.quote: anthropoid primates may have generalized the bonding processes that characterize monogamous pairbonds to other non-reproductive relationships ('friendships'), thereby giving rise to the quantitative relationship between group size and brain size that we find in this taxon.
494.content: Anthropoid primates generalized the bonding processes that characterize monogamous pair-bonds to non-reproductive relationships (friendships), creating a unique quantitative brain-group size relationship not seen in any other taxon. This explains why primate sociality is qualitatively different from all other mammals.
494.where: Annals of Human Biology 36(5):562-572, central argument. DOI: 10.1080/03014460902960289

495.quote: the demands of behavioural coordination that are the more likely
495.content: The primary cognitive cost of pair-bonding is behavioral coordination and synchrony (scheduling, conflict resolution, spatial proximity maintenance), not mate choice optimization. This coordination demand requires perspective-taking capacities that may have provided the substrate for theory of mind.
495.where: Annals of Human Biology 36(5):562-572, Table I and discussion. DOI: 10.1080/03014460902960289

496.content: The phase shift from qualitative (pair-bonding) to quantitative (group-size) social brain processing likely occurred in the Eocene, coinciding with dietary shifts from insectivory to frugivory that may have created ecological conditions favoring larger social groups in early primates.
496.where: Annals of Human Biology 36(5):562-572, evolutionary timing section. DOI: 10.1080/03014460902960289

497.quote: recent analyses suggest that it may have been the particular demands of the more intense forms of pairbonding that was the critical factor that triggered this evolutionary development
497.content: Across five vertebrate taxa (carnivores, ungulates, bats, birds, primates), pair-bonded species consistently have larger relative brain sizes than non-pair-bonded species. Fisher combined probability test: chi-squared(10)=48.04, p<<0.001. The effect holds even excluding primates: chi-squared(8)=46.42, p<0.001.
497.where: Science 317(5843):1344-1347, DOI: 10.1126/science.1145463. PMID: 17823343. Companion data in Shultz & Dunbar 2007 Proc B (PMC2274976).

498.quote: Primate sociality is based on bonded relationships of a kind that are found only in pairbonds in other taxa.
498.content: Primates are the sole exception to the pair-bonding rule: only in primates does group size (not pair-bonding) predict brain size. Strong positive correlation between group size and brain size in primates (lambda=0.80, F(1,40)=8.14, p<0.01). No such relationship in carnivores (p=0.80) or artiodactyls (p=0.58).
498.where: Science 317(5843):1344-1347 and Shultz & Dunbar 2007 Proc B (PMC2274976), PGLS analysis

499.content: In birds, lifelong pair-bonds (not annual re-pairing) predict larger brains. Bi-parental care does not drive the effect. The cognitive demand is specifically about maintaining long-term bonded relationships, not mate choice or parental coordination per se.
499.where: Science 317(5843):1344-1347 and Shultz & Dunbar 2007 Proc B, bird analysis

500.quote: the everyday relationships of anthropoid primates involve a form of 'bondedness' that is only found elsewhere in reproductive pairbonds.
500.content: Anthropoid primates co-opted pair-bond bonding mechanisms for group-level social relationships. The everyday relationships of anthropoid primates involve a form of bondedness found only in reproductive pair-bonds in other taxa. This unique generalization created qualitatively different primate sociality.

501.quote: These results undermine conventional notions of what constitutes social complexity. Indeed, we doubt that many would have seriously suggested that pairbonded social systems are more complex (and by implication, more cognitively demanding) than large polygamous or promiscuously mating groups.
501.content: Anthropoid primates differ significantly from all other taxa in proportion of species with bonded social structure (chi-squared(2)=8.49, p=0.01). Strepsirhine primates do NOT differ from ungulates and carnivores (chi-squared(2)=1.89, p=0.39). The bonding generalization is specific to anthropoids, not all primates.
501.where: Shultz & Dunbar 2007 Proc B (PMC2274976), bonded relationships analysis

502.quote: Each layer increases relationship numbers by an approximate multiple of 3 (5-15-50-150) but decreasing levels of intimacy (strong, medium, and weak ties) and frequency of interaction.
502.content: Personal social networks consist of hierarchically inclusive nested layers of approximately 5/15/50/150 individuals, each layer roughly 3x the previous. Support group (~5): individuals from whom one would seek personal advice in severe distress. Sympathy group (~15): people whose sudden death would be greatly upsetting, contacted at least monthly. Affinity group (~50): casual but close friends. Active network (~150): total recognized and annually interacted with.
502.where: British Journal of Psychology 103(2):149-168. DOI: 10.1111/j.2044-8295.2011.02061.x. PMID: 22506741. Abstract-limited.

503.quote: At each layer, the benefits are asymptotic but the costs of maintaining a relationship at that level (most obviously, the time that has to be invested in servicing it) are roughly linear with the number of relationships.
503.content: At each social layer, the benefits of adding more relationships are asymptotic (diminishing returns), while the costs of maintenance - primarily time - are roughly linear with relationship count. The intersection of these curves creates natural breakpoints that generate the layered structure. This is a cost-benefit explanation for why Dunbar layers exist.
503.where: British Journal of Psychology 103(2):149-168. DOI: 10.1111/j.2044-8295.2011.02061.x. Abstract-limited.

504.content: Approximately 40% of available social time is devoted to the innermost 5 people (support clique), and another 20% to the next 10 (completing the sympathy group of 15). Two-thirds of total social time goes to just 15 people, despite having ~150 in the active network.
504.where: British Journal of Psychology 103(2):149-168, citing Roberts et al and other empirical sources

505.quote: psychologically, these trade-offs are related to the level of trust in a relationship, and that this is itself a function of the time invested in the relationship.
505.content: Trust is the proximal psychological mechanism mediating social layer structure. Trade-offs at each layer are related to the level of trust in a relationship, and trust is itself a function of time invested. Trust operates as a cognitive heuristic that calibrates relationship investment to expected reciprocity at each layer.

506.quote: The social brain hypothesis has suggested that natural social network sizes may have a characteristic size in humans. This is determined in part by cognitive constraints and in part by the time costs of servicing relationships.
506.content: Mean Facebook friend count matches Dunbar's number prediction. Sample 1 (N=2000, nationally stratified UK): mean=155.2 friends (z=0.20, p=0.842 vs prediction of 150, 95% CI=100-200). Sample 2 (N=1375, nationally stratified UK professionals): mean=182.8 (z=1.29, p=0.198). Only 14.2% and 13.4% respectively had more than 300 friends.
506.where: Royal Society Open Science 3(1):150292. DOI: 10.1098/rsos.150292. PMID: 26909163. PMC4736918. Full open-access text.

507.quote: We can only interact coherently with a very small number of other people (about three, in fact) at any one time.
507.content: Online inner social layers replicate offline sizes exactly. Support clique (crisis contacts): mean=4.1, not significantly different from offline values of 3.8+/-2.29 (z=0.13, p=0.897) or generic value of 5 (z=0.39, p=0.694). Sympathy group (close friends): mean=13.6, not different from 11.3+/-6.19 (z=0.37, p=0.711) or 15 (z=0.23, p=0.818).
507.where: Royal Society Open Science 3(1):150292, inner layer analysis

508.quote: On average, respondents in Sample 1 considered that only 27.6% of their Facebook friends could be considered 'genuine' (i.e. close) friends, with a strong modal value between 0 and 10%.
508.content: Only 27.6% of Facebook friends are considered genuine (close) friends, with a strong modal value between 0 and 10%. Large online networks add only loose acquaintances, not close friends. People with unusually large networks do not increase close friendships but add weakly-defined acquaintances.
508.where: Royal Society Open Science 3(1):150292, genuine friends analysis

509.quote: it may be that face-to-face meetings are required from time to time to prevent friendships, in particular, sliding down through the network layers and eventually slipping over the edge of the 150 layer into the category of acquaintances.
509.content: Face-to-face contact is required to prevent friendships from decaying through the network layers and eventually becoming mere acquaintances. Social media may slow the natural rate of decay but cannot substitute for in-person interaction. This directly confirms that the bonding system requires physical co-presence that technology cannot replace.

510.quote: social media may function mainly to prevent friendships decaying over time in the absence of opportunities for face-to-face contact.
510.content: Age strongly predicts total network size (r=-0.972, p=0.006) with 18-24 year olds averaging 282 friends, but inner layers show minimal age variation (support clique: r=-0.837, p=0.077; sympathy group: r=-0.042, p=0.947). The cognitive/time constraint on intimate relationships is stable across ages even as total network size varies.
510.where: Royal Society Open Science 3(1):150292, age effects analysis

511.quote: Dunbar (1998), for example, documented that primate brain size correlates most strongly not with primates' physical ecology but, rather, with their social group size (as a proxy for social complexity).
511.content: Tomasello cites Dunbar 1998: primate brain size correlates most strongly not with physical ecology but with social group size (as proxy for social complexity). Primates' social cognition is aimed mainly at competition (Machiavellian intelligence) - tracking dominance and affiliative relationships that affect competition for food and mates. This frames Dunbar's cognitive constraint as operating specifically through competitive social tracking.
511.where: A Natural History of Human Thinking (2014), pp. 76-77 (lines 2987-2996 in text file)

512.quote: group size is only a very gross indicator of social complexity (Dunbar focuses on the greater numbers of social relationships and reputations to be kept track of), and brain size is only a very gross indicator of cognitive capacities, so the social brain hypothesis gives us only a very general indication of the actual processes involved on either side of the correlation.
512.content: Tomasello discusses the social brain hypothesis as supporting evidence for the evolution of human cooperation. Gowlett et al. (2012) traced brain-group size correlation across human evolution and found an especially big jump at ~400kya (Homo heidelbergensis), coinciding with Tomasello's hypothesized joint intentionality transition. However, Tomasello notes the hypothesis provides only a very general indication: group size is a gross indicator of social complexity and brain size a gross indicator of cognitive capacities.
512.where: A Natural History of Human Thinking (2014), pp. 133-134 (lines 5168-5185 in text file)

513.content: Henrich cites Dunbar 1998 on the social brain hypothesis in the context of arguing that human intelligence is collective rather than individual. Endnote references place Dunbar alongside Byrne and Whiten (1992) and Humphrey (1976) as proponents of the Machiavellian intelligence view that Henrich then challenges: cultural evolution, not individual social cognition, is what makes humans smart. Group size matters for Henrich primarily as a driver of cumulative cultural complexity, not through Dunbar's cognitive constraint mechanism.
513.where: The Secret of Our Success (2016), endnotes 7 and 19 (lines 12444, 12498), main text ch. 2 and ch. 12

514.quote: Humans' large neocortex is an obvious possibility. Not only do human mothers need more help getting big-brained babies through narrow birth canals but they are better able to evaluate the costs and benefits of their own behavior.
514.content: Hrdy cites Dunbar & Shultz (2007) on the correlation between large brain size and long juvenile/adolescent life phases. The neocortex discussion in Mothers and Others frames brain evolution through alloparenting: humans' large neocortex enables evaluation of allomaternal trustworthiness, while also creating the extended dependency that necessitates cooperative breeding. This connects Dunbar's social brain to Hrdy's cooperative breeding hypothesis as complementary explanations.
514.where: Mothers and Others (2009), endnotes ch. 8 note 4 (line 13045), main text pp. 39-40 (lines 1580-1614, 1795-1801, 2940-2943)

515.content: Plant growth is often constrained by the scarcest essential nutrient in the soil, not by the average availability of nutrients. Adding more of an abundant nutrient does not, on its own, fully compensate for deficiency in a scarce one. Cor adopts the structural form of this claim as a heuristic for mechanism resolution: well-being is often bottlenecked by severe unresolved deficits in individual mechanisms and is not well described as a simple average across mechanism states. The agronomy content does not transfer; the bottleneck framing does. Cross-system buffering effects do exist in the human architecture (handled by DA3), so this is a heuristic about bottlenecks, not a claim of strict biochemical non-substitutability.
515.where: Passim (the Law of the Minimum is the central thesis of the work)

516.quote: It has become increasingly clear during the past half century that primary-process affective mechanisms are concentrated in ancient subcortical midline brain regions that are anatomically and neurochemically, and hence, evolutionarily, similar in all mammalian species.
516.content: Seven distinct emotional systems identified with specific neuroanatomy and neurochemistry: SEEKING (VTA/NAcc/lateral hypothalamus, DA+), RAGE (medial amygdala→BNST→hypothalamus→PAG, substance P+), FEAR (central amygdala→hypothalamus→dorsal PAG, glutamate+/CRF+), LUST (cortico-medial amygdala/BNST/preoptic, steroids+), CARE (anterior cingulate/BNST/preoptic/VTA, oxytocin+/prolactin+), PANIC (anterior cingulate/BNST/dorsomedial thalamus/PAG, opioids−/oxytocin−/CRF+), PLAY (dorsomedial diencephalon/parafascicular/PAG, opioids+/−). Each mapped in Fig. 2 with specific neurochemical modulators.
516.where: Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 35(9):1791-1804, p. 1795, Fig. 2. DOI: 10.1016/j.neubiorev.2011.08.003

517.quote: When we artificially activate brain emotion-behavior generating circuits, animals rapidly learn to turn off ESB that evokes fear- and anger-type responses, and they turn on brain stimulation that generates playful sounds, exploration, sexual eagerness and maternal care.
517.content: Electrical brain stimulation (ESB) of specific subcortical regions produces coherent emotional behaviors in all mammals tested. Animals given control over ESB self-select: they turn off stimulation evoking fear/anger responses and turn on stimulation generating playful sounds, exploration, sexual eagerness, and maternal care. This reward/punishment valence demonstrates genuine affective experience, not mere behavioral reflexes.

518.quote: Clearly lesions of higher areas do not diminish the emotional responses from lower areas, while damage to lower areas can dramatically compromise emotional actions generated from higher areas.
518.content: Lower subcortical regions, especially the periaqueductal gray (PAG), are more important for generating emotional feelings than cortical regions. Three key properties of the PAG: (1) lowest ESB energy to obtain powerful emotional changes, (2) smallest brain damage compromising consciousness, (3) most massive convergence of brain emotional systems. Lesions of higher areas do not diminish emotional responses from lower areas, while damage to lower areas dramatically compromises emotional actions generated from higher areas.

519.quote: Never have such profound emotional states been provoked by stimulating neocortical regions.
519.content: All seven emotional systems survive radical neo-decortication (complete surgical removal of the cerebral cortex). Decorticate animals retain all emotional-instinctual urges intact, though their capacity to learn new instrumental behaviors is severely impaired. ESB of subcortical regions in humans produces intense affective experiences; neocortical stimulation never produces such emotional states.

520.quote: When made hungry for play, rats pounce on each other, engendering bouts of chasing and wrestling, all accompanied by joyful 50 kHz chirps signaling an intense social joy.
520.content: Rats produce 50-kHz ultrasonic chirps during play that are homologous to human laughter. These joyful sounds are most abundant during rough-and-tumble play and human-administered tickling. The affective valence is confirmed by approach behavior and conditioned place preferences. This demonstrates that positive social affect is a fundamental feature of mammalian brain organization, not a human-unique construction.

521.content: Three convergent lines of evidence demonstrate subcortical affective states: (i) mammals are attracted to the same environmental rewards and drugs of abuse as humans; (ii) human emotional feelings depend on subcortical brain systems where evolutionarily homologous instinctual neural systems exist; (iii) artificial activations of deep brain emotional systems are liked and disliked by animals, as measured by approach and avoidance measures.

522.quote: These criteria have been fulfilled or approximated for a variety of brain systems that exist in all mammals studied so far.
522.content: Three empirical criteria for determining existence of emotional feelings in animals, all fulfilled: (1) neural circuits must exist that activate coherent emotional behaviors, (2) artificial arousal of such systems must generate conditioned approach/escape/avoidance, (3) key neurochemistries and brain activation patterns must correlate with predicted affective changes in humans. These criteria have been fulfilled for multiple brain systems across all mammals studied.

523.quote: Those who are not willing to give animals any consciousness are probably thinking about the tertiary human-typical linguistic variants. They may also be generalizing too readily from human perceptual consciousness, which is clearly dependent on neocortical functions, to an affective consciousness whose locus of control is largely sub-neocortical.
523.content: Three levels of consciousness: primary-process (raw sensory/emotional feelings, subcortical), secondary (thoughts about experiences via perceptual images, learning/memory), and tertiary (thoughts about thoughts, awareness of awareness, largely human-specific, requires neocortical linguistic-symbolic processing). Affective consciousness is primary-process and subcortical; those who deny animal consciousness are thinking about tertiary cortical variants and generalizing from perceptual consciousness to affective consciousness.

524.quote: The guiding evolutionary concept was that neural systems that elaborate social attachments have evolutionary relations with those that mediate the affective qualities of physical pain, including modulation by the same chemistries such as endogenous opioids.
524.content: PANIC/separation-distress system evolved from physical pain mechanisms. Social attachments are mediated by the same neurochemistry as physical pain, particularly endogenous opioids. The PAG is the brain area from which emotional distress is most readily evoked in both humans and animals with the lowest ESB levels. Social exclusion and depression activate anterior cingulate regions known to regulate pain.

525.quote: phenomenal affective consciousness is not simply a 'read-out' function of the neocortex. That view of emotional feelings is only a small part of the story, and hence deeply flawed as a major explanation
525.content: Phenomenal affective consciousness is not a cortical readout function. Emotional affects are critically linked to the dynamics of instinctual emotional action apparatus, which can be regulated but not created by higher cortico-cognitive activities. Play behavior survives radical decortication: animals without any neocortex play vigorously. Human children with severe higher brain damage exhibit rich affective lives when reared in loving environments.

526.quote: depression is intimately related to 1) sustained overactivity of the separation-distress PANIC system that can, if prolonged, lead to a downward cascade of psychological despair (a theoretical view originally formulated by John Bowlby); and 2) the despair phase that follows the acute PANIC response which is characterized by abnormally low activity of the SEEKING system.
526.content: Two-phase model of depression genesis: (1) sustained overactivity of the PANIC/GRIEF separation-distress system produces psychological pain, followed by (2) abnormally low SEEKING system activity during the despair phase. The initial agitated panic state transitions to shutdown when reunification attempts fail, paralleling Bowlby's protest-despair sequence.

527.quote: Depression may feel bad because brain separation-distress systems create psychological pain.
527.content: PANIC/GRIEF circuitry maps directly onto brain targets for treatment-resistant depression: starts in the PAG, ascends through dorsomedial thalamus, and terminates in subcallosal anterior cingulate - the same regions targeted by deep brain stimulation (Mayberg et al., 2005). Key neurochemistry: declining opioids and oxytocin, elevated CRF, increased glutamate. Dynorphin mediates SEEKING shutdown as a distinct form of negative affect.

528.quote: The pain of depression -- arising mostly from social loss and social defeat -- may be the price we mammals pay for the evolutionary advantages of social bonds that enrich our lives and promote procreation and survival.
528.content: The pain of depression arises from the evolutionary price of social bonds: PANIC/GRIEF evolved from general pain mechanisms (birds possess a homologous system). This psychic-pain system promotes social cohesion, forges bonds between infants and caretakers, and fortifies friendships and sexual relationships. Depression is the cost mammals pay for the survival advantages of social bonds.

529.quote: It is becoming harder to believe that general brain serotonergic and/or noradrenergic changes, which globally regulate aspects of forebrain arousal and dynamics, will specifically explain the morbid moods of depression.
529.content: SSRIs have modest overall efficacy (STAR*D findings); serotonin and norepinephrine regulate general arousal, not the specific affect of depression. More targeted interventions include ultra-low-dose buprenorphine (which both activates mu-opioid receptors and blocks despair-promoting dynorphin/kappa receptors), oxytocin, CRF antagonists, and glutamate modulators (ketamine). Psychotherapeutic activation of CARE and PLAY systems remains almost completely untapped.

530.quote: Current neurobehavioral evidence indicates that there are at least four executive circuits of this type -- those which elaborate central states of expectancy, rage, fear, and panic.
530.content: Four primary emotional executive circuits identified via electrical brain stimulation: expectancy (later renamed SEEKING), rage, fear, and panic. Each is a transhypothalamic command circuit that concurrently activates behavioral action patterns, physiological responses, and subjective states. These circuits developed early in mammalian brain evolution and the underlying control mechanisms remain similar across species.

531.quote: Emotions seem to arise ultimately from hard-wired neural circuits in the visceral-limbic brain that facilitate diverse and adaptive behavioral and physiological responses to major classes of environmental challenges.
531.content: Emotions arise from hard-wired neural circuits in the visceral-limbic brain, not from cortical constructions. These circuits facilitate diverse adaptive responses to major classes of environmental challenges. Theoretically guided studies of the animal brain can reveal how primitive emotions are organized in the human brain, and conversely, human introspective access can generate hypotheses for animal brain research.

532.content: Psychiatric disorders may arise from dysfunctional activity in the same emotional command circuits that generate normal emotions. Learning processes interact with these circuits, with emotional arousals gating sensory inputs and programming higher cognitive activities. The manner in which learning and psychiatric disorders arise from circuit activities is explored.

533.quote: Existing results suggest the operation of a harmoniously operating brain process which generates a unique emotive brain process that is appropriately referred to as social play.
533.content: Social play in juvenile rats constitutes a distinct emotional brain process with dedicated neural circuitry, not a byproduct of other systems. Play can be experimentally controlled via social deprivation and objectively quantified through pinning behavior (one rat pinning another during rough-and-tumble play). The underlying circuits may reveal how complex behavioral competence arises ontogenetically and yield clues to the genesis of psychopathologies.

534.content: Neurochemical substrates of play include the endogenous opioid system: morphine (mu-opioid agonist) increases play, naloxone (opioid antagonist) reduces play. Brain regions critical for play include the parafascicular area (PFA) of the thalamus (lesions reduced pinning by 73%) and dorsomedial thalamus (lesions reduced pinning by 33%). Play circuitry positions rigorous neural analysis as the route to empirical definition of play.
534.where: Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 8(4):465-492, neurochemical substrates section. Follow-up data from Siviy & Panksepp 1985 (PMID: 3038140)

535.content: Positive affect has at least two distinct neural substrates: appetitive (anticipatory) positive affect mediated by ventral striatal dopamine systems (SEEKING), and consummatory positive affect (sensory pleasure) mediated by dopamine-independent opioid and GABA receptors in ventral striatum, amygdala, and orbital frontal cortex. Various neuropeptides mediate homeostatic satisfactions as a third category.

536.content: 50-kHz ultrasonic chirping in rats is the most robust during rough-and-tumble play and experimenter-administered tickling (which elicits more chirps than self-initiated play). Young animals prefer adults that chirp abundantly over those that chirp infrequently. Animals will run mazes and press levers to get tickled (operant reinforcement). Approach latency correlates with chirp rate (r=0.80, p<0.001). The chirping response can be selectively bred within four generations, demonstrating genetic basis.
536.where: Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 30(2):173-187. Supporting data from Panksepp & Burgdorf 2003 (Physiology & Behavior 79:533-547, open-access)

537.quote: contact comfort is a variable of overwhelming importance in the development of affectional response, whereas lactation is a variable of negligible importance.
537.content: Contact comfort overwhelms lactation as determinant of infant attachment. Infant rhesus monkeys spent 17-18 hours/day on cloth-covered surrogate mother vs ~1 hour on wire mother, regardless of which mother provided milk. No measurable difference between cloth-fed and wire-fed groups in cloth preference. 8 newborn monkeys in dual-surrogate condition tested over 165+ consecutive days.
537.where: American Psychologist 13:673-685. Full text at psychclassics.yorku.ca/Harlow/love.htm

538.quote: The wire mother is biologically adequate but psychologically inept.
