But human children develop robust theory of mind in cooperative contexts - because in a cooperatively breeding species, infants who could read the intentions of multiple caregivers had a survival advantage. Human mind-reading evolved not for competition but for navigating the cooperative breeding network.

findings.quote: This is an elaboration of, but entirely consistent with, my hypothesis that what is important 1s control and opportunities to participate fully in society. The effort/reward model implies that lack of reward means lack of full participation. In the Siegrist model, lack of appropriate reward for effort expended causes emotional distress and activates biological stress pathways, with consequences for disease.
findings.content: Marmot integrates Siegrist's effort/reward model into his control/participation hypothesis by treating 'reward' (esteem, recognition, appropriate return for effort) as a mode of full social participation. Lack of appropriate reward therefore maps onto the same autonomy/participation pathway that drives the health gradient; it is not a third distinct factor but an extension of the participation axis through the workplace reciprocity channel.
findings.where: Chapter 5 'Who's in Charge?' pp. 131-132 synthesizing Karasek + Siegrist

findings.content: Miller frames consumer signaling specifically around the "Central Six" personality dimensions: general intelligence plus the Big Five (openness, conscientiousness, agreeableness, stability, extraversion). These are the traits consumers attempt to display via purchases, and personality research on the Big Five is presented as directly applicable to consumer behavior. This gives a specific mapping: consumer goods = signaling vehicles for Central Six traits = proxies for mate-choice and friend-selection mechanisms that evolved to read these traits in conspecifics.

Ancestral work was characteristically small-group, embodied, skill-based, and autonomy-rich. Psychological adaptations for work - cognitive mechanisms for toolmaking, resource acquisition, learning, and cooperative production - evolved in the context of small networks of hunter-gatherers where effort-outcome links were visible and physical.

Digital work exacerbates evolutionary mismatch through multiple simultaneous channels: sedentarism replacing embodied activity, always-on connectivity disrupting circadian boundaries, electronic surveillance replacing autonomy, remote/distributed work weakening face-to-face social bonds, and abstract screen-mediated tasks replacing tangible effort-outcome feedback. These mismatches are predicted to increase chronic work stress and related physical and mental health problems.

Organizational interventions for digital work should be grounded in mismatch logic: restore movement breaks, protect circadian boundaries (right to disconnect), design for team sizes within Dunbar-range cooperation thresholds, increase decision latitude and visible effort-outcome links, and create physical co-presence opportunities for distributed teams.

findings.quote: Contact with disgust elicitors, real or imagined, is associated with (i) a characteristic facial expression... (ii) behaviour patterns that include withdrawal, distancing, stopping or dropping the object of disgust... (iii) physiological changes including lowered blood pressure and galvanic skin response.
findings.content: Disgust elicitors are universal across cultures: bodily wastes, body contents, sick/deformed/dead/unhygienic people. Contact with disgust elicitors produces a characteristic facial expression, withdrawal/distancing behaviors, and physiological changes including lowered blood pressure and galvanic skin response. Brain imaging reveals a specific neural disgust network including anterior insular cortex, basal ganglia, and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex. All societies demonstrate individual and group-level hygiene behaviors.

Disgust sensitivity is adaptively calibrated to current physiological vulnerability. Women show increased disgust during the first trimester of pregnancy when the immune system is suppressed to tolerate paternal genetic material in the blastocyst. Salivary progesterone correlates positively with disgust sensitivity in normally cycling women - progesterone being the endocrine cue for immune downregulation. Opiate users, whose immune systems are pharmacologically suppressed, make fewer errors identifying disgust faces. Conversely, hunger downregulates disgust for food specifically while maintaining disgust for other pathogen cues - 15 hours of food deprivation reduced facial expressions of disgust to food but not to body wastes.

Females consistently score substantially higher on measures of disgust sensitivity than males across cultures. This sex difference likely reflects women's evolutionary history of responsibility for childcare - women need to be 'disgusted enough for two people' to keep dependent children free of disease. Disgust sensitivity is heritable and shows stable individual trait variation associated with neuroticism. Social learning modulates disgust in both directions: a 15-second verbal and visual display of disgust toward a novel object reduced infants' contact with the object for at least 1 hour in 14-month-olds, while positive attitudes by adults dissipated avoidance behaviors. The 'copy the frequent' heuristic for hygiene behavior can perpetuate either healthy or unhealthy practices.

The behavioral immune system's functional flexibility operates at both individual and societal levels. At the individual level, people with chronically higher 'germ aversion' report chronically lower extraversion, and pathogen salience causes reduced extraversion and avoidant motor movements toward pictures of people. At the societal level, countries with higher historical pathogen prevalence show lower population-level extraversion, lower openness to experience, and higher collectivism. The culinary spice usage pattern illustrates this: spices are natural antibiotics, and their use in food preparation is more common under ecological circumstances of high pathogen prevalence, reflecting the cost-benefit calculus of pathogen defense across populations.

At a population level, cross-national data show higher historical pathogen prevalence predicts lower extraversion, lower openness to experience, and higher collectivism (r=0.73 for collectivism-pathogen correlation, Fincher et al. 2008), with correlations surviving controls for latitude, climate, and socioeconomic status. Culinary spice usage illustrates the population-level cost-benefit calculus: spices are natural antibiotics, and their use in food preparation is more common under ecological circumstances of high pathogen prevalence. Women in first trimester of pregnancy show heightened ethnocentrism and xenophobia (Navarrete et al. 2007), consistent with upregulated behavioral immune responses during adaptive immunosuppression.

Meta-analysis of 50 studies (published and unpublished) testing whether incidental disgust amplifies moral judgment. Raw effect: d=0.11 (small), strongest for gustatory/olfactory induction. After correcting for publication bias, the effect disappears entirely (d=-0.01). Prevalent confounds mean d=0.11 is an upper bound. The finding that the incidental disgust amplification effect may be artifactual challenges strong claims about emotion causally driving moral judgment and suggests the Haidt and Wheatley 2005 disgust-priming finding may not generalize robustly.

findings.quote: Disgust is an evolved psychological system for protecting organisms from infection through disease avoidant behaviour. This 'behavioural immune system', present in a diverse array of species, exhibits universal features that orchestrate hygienic behaviour in response to cues of risk of contact with pathogens.
findings.content: Disgust is an evolved psychological system for protecting organisms from infection through disease-avoidant behavior. This behavioral immune system is present in diverse species and exhibits universal features that orchestrate hygienic behavior in response to cues of pathogen contact risk. Three specialized learning mechanisms modify the disgust response: the Garcia effect (one-trial aversion learning), evaluative conditioning, and the law of contagion.

Disgust operates as a multi-level adaptive system for disease avoidance with three distinct learning mechanisms that tune innate responses to local environments. The Garcia effect flags foods as aversive after illness. Evaluative conditioning creates stable disgust labels when a powerful disgust reaction transfers to previously neutral stimuli - these labels are 'quickly acquired and slow to fade.' The law of contagion tracks pathogen spread by flagging any object touched by a disgusting stimulus, though these labels are temporary and item-specific. All three mechanisms allow the disgust system to respond to the local pathogen environment without requiring direct detection of microscopic organisms.

Group hygiene behavior extends disgust from biological function to symbolic cultural regulation. Washing rituals took on symbolic significance in Semitic, Greek, Hindu, Buddhist, Islamic, and Christian religions. Hindu scripture (Laws of Manu, c. 200 BCE) prescribes avoidance of 12 bodily impurities and extends this logic to create caste separations - people whose work involves contact with 'polluting' substances become a separate and 'impure' caste. Dietary laws similarly extend biologically reasonable food avoidances to whole new classes of animals, with adherence serving as group-demarcating symbols. The emotional resources of disgust and contagion sustain these social separations, making violation a moral transgression rather than merely a hygiene failure.

The behavioral immune system comprises evolved psychological mechanisms that detect cues of infectious pathogens and trigger disgust-mediated avoidance responses. Operating on the 'smoke detector principle,' it minimizes costly false-negative errors (missing real pathogens) at the cost of many false-positive errors -- generating aversive responses to people with physical disabilities, obesity, elderly appearance, or foreign ethnicity who pose no actual infection risk. The system exhibits functional flexibility: responses intensify when perceivers feel more vulnerable to infection (e.g., women in first trimester of pregnancy show heightened ethnocentrism and xenophobia; Navarrete et al., 2007). At a population level, cross-national data show that higher historical pathogen prevalence predicts lower extraversion, lower openness to experience, and higher collectivism (r = 0.73 for collectivism-pathogen correlation; Fincher et al., 2008), with correlations surviving controls for confounds. Mere visual perception of diseased-looking people triggers perceivers' white blood cells to mount more vigorous antibacterial responses, suggesting behavioral and physiological immune systems interact.

The behavioral immune system operates on the smoke detector principle: it minimizes costly false-negative errors (missing real pathogens) at the cost of many false-positive errors - generating aversive responses to people with physical disabilities, obesity, elderly appearance, or foreign ethnicity who pose no actual infection risk. The system exhibits functional flexibility: responses intensify when perceivers feel more vulnerable to infection. Mere visual perception of diseased-looking people triggers perceivers white blood cells to mount more vigorous antibacterial responses (interleukin-6 upregulation), demonstrating that behavioral and physiological immune systems interact bidirectionally. This cross-talk means that simply SEEING signs of disease activates actual immune defenses.

findings.quote: We contrast this signaling view with the idea that moral disgust has a function in causing people to avoid some set of objects, behaviors, or people, as is the case with pathogen and sexual disgust.
findings.content: Tybur et al.'s evolutionary-computational framework treats pathogen, sexual, and moral disgust as three FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT adaptations with distinct information-processing systems, not one mechanism misfiring. Moral disgust is theorized as a condemnation-coordination/signaling adaptation (building on DeScioli & Kurzban) that shares with pathogen disgust primarily the EXPRESSIVE (facial/vocal) component; the defining pathogen "do not touch"/avoidance motivation is absent - moral disgust instead covaries with approach-motivated anger and the desire to punish. The authors explicitly contrast their signaling account with the view that moral disgust functions to cause avoidance "as is the case with pathogen and sexual disgust," and flag the moral domain as the least settled of the three ("little consensus about the measurement, function, and even existence"; treatment "necessarily more exploratory"). Their one causal claim - that activating pathogen/sexual disgust raises moral-wrongness judgments - is framed as disgust being ONE limited input to a SEPARATE strategic rule-endorsement system ("we do not suggest that disgust serves as an input to every moral judgment"), and is evidenced by the Schnall/Eskine/Wheatley-Haidt/Moretti priming studies that Landy & Goodwin (2015, ext105) meta-analyze to d≈-0.01 after publication-bias correction. Net: the canonical framework supports a shared-machinery / functionally-distinct reading and does NOT establish moral disgust as a confirmed lower rung of the pathogen-disgust mechanism - confirming M12's moral-tier demotion while authoritatively grounding the three-domain disgust structure.
findings.where: Psychological Review 120(1):65-84. Quote from "Disgust as Output of Moral Cognition" subsection (p. 76). Three-domain thesis: Abstract (p. 65) and "An Evolutionary View of Emotion" (p. 67).

findings.quote: As expected, physical activity level, PAL, was greater among Hadza foragers than among Westerners. Nonetheless, average daily energy expenditure of traditional Hadza foragers was no different than that of Westerners after controlling for body size. The metabolic cost of walking and resting were also similar among Hadza and Western groups. The similarity in metabolic rates across a broad range of cultures challenges current models of obesity suggesting that Western lifestyles lead to decreased energy expenditure.
findings.content: The Pontzer 2012 Hadza-energetics finding: despite dramatically greater physical activity (Hadza PAL ~1.78-2.26 vs Western PAL ~1.68-1.81), Hadza hunter-gatherers expend no more total daily energy than Western adults after controlling for body size. The metabolic cost of walking and resting are also similar across groups. This contradicted the then-dominant obesity hypothesis that Western lifestyles reduce caloric expenditure and motivated the Constrained TEE model developed in subsequent work. The implication: global obesity cannot be explained by Western sedentarism producing lower daily energy expenditure - Western and hunter-gatherer daily calorie burns are similar, so the obesity difference must lie primarily in energy intake and food composition.
findings.where: Pontzer et al. 2012 PLoS ONE 7(7):e40503, Abstract

findings.content: Moss documents how the food industry systematically optimizes products for the "bliss point" - the precise concentration of sugar, fat, and salt that maximizes sensory pleasure and craving. Howard Moskowitz, a mathematician and experimental psychologist, built a consulting empire on this optimization: "I've optimized soups, I've optimized pizzas, I've optimized salad dressings and pickles." His method involves creating dozens of product variations, testing them on consumers, then using regression analysis to identify the exact formulation that generates "the biggest crave." Australian psychologist Robert McBride described the bliss point at an industry conference: "Humans like sweetness, but how much sweetness? For all ingredients in food and drink, there is an optimum concentration at which the sensory pleasure is maximal. This optimum level is called the bliss point. The bliss point is a powerful phenomenon and dictates what we eat and drink more than we realize."

Moss reveals through internal industry sources that food companies knowingly engineer products to exploit evolved taste preferences and are aware of the overconsumption consequences. At a secret 1999 meeting of eleven food industry CEOs, Pillsbury executive James Behnke confronted them with "the notion that they and their companies had played a central role in creating this health crisis." Industry insider Michael Mudd presented slides showing the driver of obesity was the "ubiquity of inexpensive, good-tasting, super-sized, energy-dense foods" - the very products these companies staked their success on. Kraft executive Bob Ruff acknowledged that formulating foods to be irresistible was "in constant discussion" internally: "You're looking for the product that people like best." Yet when Kraft proposed internal caps on salt, sugar, and fat in 2003, other companies resisted - General Mills CEO Stephen Sanger told the assembled executives that consumers were not "asking us to put less sugar in." Revenue structures depended on maximizing consumption of products the industry's own scientists knew exploited natural cravings.

findings.quote: SBT suggests that proximity to social resources decreases the cost of climbing both the literal and figurative hills we face, because the brain construes social resources as bioenergetic resources, much like oxygen or glucose. Indeed, evidence suggests that hills literally appear less steep when standing next to a friend. Moreover, socially isolated individuals consume more sugar, even after adjusting for body mass index, weight related self-image, depression, physical activity, educational level, age and income. To the human brain, social and metabolic resources are treated almost interchangeably.
findings.content: Social Baseline Theory suggests that proximity to social resources decreases the cost of climbing both the literal and figurative hills we face, because the brain construes social resources as bioenergetic resources, much like oxygen or glucose. Evidence suggests that hills literally appear less steep when standing next to a friend. Moreover, socially isolated individuals consume more sugar, even after adjusting for body mass index, weight-related self-image, depression, physical activity, educational level, age, and income. To the human brain, social and metabolic resources are treated almost interchangeably.
findings.where: Section 'Social relationships decrease the predicted cost of the environment,' p. 88

findings.quote: Although there is much variation, PALs of hunter-gatherers average 1.9 for men and 1.8 for women, slightly below PAL scores for subsistence farmers, which average 2.1 for men and 1.9 for women. To put these values into context, hunter-gatherer PALs are about the same as those of factory workers and farmers in the developed world (1.8), and about 15 percent higher than PALs of people with desk jobs in developed countries (1.6). In other words, typical hunter-gatherers are about as physically active as Americans or Europeans who include about an hour of exercise in their daily routine. In case you are wondering, most mammals in the wild have PALs of 3.3 or more, nearly twice as high as hunter-gatherers. Thus, comparatively speaking, humans who must hunt and gather all the food they eat and make everything they own by hand are substantially less active than average free-ranging mammals.
findings.content: Physical Activity Level (PAL) data across populations reveals the surprising result that typical hunter-gatherers are only about 15% more active than industrialized people with desk jobs - equivalent to adding one hour of walking per day to a sedentary Westerner's routine. Hunter-gatherer PALs average 1.9 (men) / 1.8 (women) vs 1.6 for desk workers. Wild mammals average PAL 3.3+, nearly twice hunter-gatherer levels. This is Lieberman's central empirical claim against 'we evolved to exercise' intuitions: humans are at the less-active end of the mammalian spectrum, and the Western sedentary gap is smaller than folk imagination assumes.
findings.where: Chapter 1 'Are We Born to Rest or Run?' pp. ~19-20

findings.content: In a large epidemiological database (n>65,000, primarily Central European), social jetlag - the discrepancy between biological circadian clock and socially imposed sleep timing - is associated with increased BMI independently of sleep duration. 69% of the population experiences at least 1 hour of social jetlag, and one-third suffers 2+ hours. Logistic regression showed social jetlag significantly increased probability of being overweight (OR=3.30, 95% CI 2.51-4.33) after controlling for age, sex, chronotype, and sleep duration. Hierarchical multiple regression revealed social jetlag positively predicts BMI in the overweight group (BMI>=25, n=20,731) with an effect size more than half that of sleep duration, but does not predict BMI in the normal weight group (BMI<25, n=43,308). Over the study period (2003-2010), chronotype progressively delayed in the population (r=0.07, p<0.001) while workday sleep duration shortened (r=-0.14, p<0.001), driven by ~80% of workers using alarm clocks. Social jetlag peaks in late adolescence due to the collision of late biological chronotype with early school start times.

Hierarchical multiple regression revealed social jetlag positively predicts BMI specifically in the overweight group (BMI>=25, n=20,731), with an effect size more than half that of sleep duration, but does NOT predict BMI in the normal weight group (BMI<25, n=43,308). Logistic regression with BMI group as outcome showed social jetlag as a significant predictor (OR=3.30, 95% CI: 2.51-4.33) of being overweight after controlling for age, sex, chronotype, and sleep duration. The differential effect by weight group suggests social jetlag may interact with metabolic vulnerability - once the system is pushed past a threshold, circadian misalignment accelerates weight gain through disrupted energy homeostasis.

findings.quote: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammation of the arterial walls that results from how you shuttle cholesterol and triglycerides (fats) around your body.
findings.content: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammation of the arterial walls resulting from how the body shuttles cholesterol and triglycerides. The process is driven by the mismatch between ancestral diet/activity patterns (which kept LDL cholesterol low and HDL high) and modern sedentary high-calorie environments that invert this ratio. Chronic arterial inflammation is a paradigm case of allostatic load from metabolic mismatch.

Ancestral human diet was characterized by: higher protein (34% vs 12% of calories), dramatically lower refined carbohydrate and sugar, higher fiber (100-150g/day vs 20g), lower sodium, higher potassium, higher micronutrient density, and near-zero processed food. Modern Western diet diverges from these parameters in almost every measurable dimension simultaneously.

findings.quote: To plot what industry insiders call the 'bliss point,' or the precise amount of sugar or fat or salt that will send consumers over the moon. At a laboratory in White Plains, New York, industry scientists who perform this alchemy walked me, step by step, through the process of engineering a new soda so that I could see the creation of bliss firsthand.
findings.content: The food industry engineers bliss points - the precise amount of sugar, fat, or salt that sends consumers over the moon. Industry scientists mathematically optimize the hedonic response curve for each product, finding the exact concentration that maximizes craving. This is not accidental food design but systematic exploitation of the reward system's response to ancestrally rare nutrient signals.

findings.quote: These were the three pillars of processed food, the creators of crave, and each of the CEOs needed them in huge quantities to turn their products into hits.
findings.content: Salt, sugar, and fat are the three pillars of processed food - the creators of crave. Each CEO needed them in huge quantities to turn products into hits. Officials discussed the power of foods to create cravings that overwhelm the best intentions of dieters. Industry-wide limits on mainline products (not just niche diet items) would be needed to diminish these cravings, but competitive pressure prevents any single company from unilaterally reducing palatability.

findings.quote: Here, we test the hypothesis that the ways in which urban populations rest, rather than the amount of time spent resting, represents an inactivity mismatch with an evolutionarily relevant hunting and gathering lifestyle, and propose that this mismatch may contribute to the negative health impacts of sedentary behavior today.
findings.content: The Inactivity Mismatch Hypothesis (Raichlen, Pontzer et al. 2020): Hadza adults spend similar amounts of time in nonambulatory rest as industrialized adults (~9.9 hours/day), but they rest in postures - squatting, kneeling, ground-sitting - that maintain higher lower-limb muscle activity than Western chair-sitting. Measured via thigh-worn accelerometers plus electromyography in the field. The hypothesis: human physiology evolved in a context of high muscle activity across the waking day BOTH through physical activity AND through resting postures with sustained low-level muscle contraction. Modern chair-sitting is the mismatch - not the total amount of rest, but the specific posture during rest.
findings.where: Raichlen, Pontzer et al. 2020 PNAS 117(13):7115-7121, Introduction

findings.quote: In addition to ground-sitting postures, Hadza individuals also spend a large percentage of their nonambulatory time in squatting (∼18%) and kneeling postures (∼12.5%) that differ from ground sitting by individuals maintaining an elevated buttocks. [...] For soleus, the assisted squat posture (squatting with heels in ground contact and with the buttocks resting on a small rock) elicited significantly higher muscle activity compared with chair sitting.
findings.content: The empirical result: Hadza adults spend roughly as much time in nonambulatory rest as industrialized adults (~9.9 hours/day for Hadza vs ~8.8 hours/day for Australian adults in comparison data), with similar average sedentary bout duration (~15 min) and similar numbers of transitions between sitting and standing per day (~50 vs ~38 for European adults). But Hadza nonambulatory time occurs heavily in squatting (~18%) and kneeling (~12.5%) postures that elicit significantly higher muscle activity than chair-sitting. The Hadza data refute the naive 'hunter-gatherers never sit' assumption and reframe the mismatch as about HOW humans rest, not HOW MUCH.
findings.where: Raichlen et al. 2020 PNAS, Results section

findings.content: The gambling industry designs for 'extinction' - continued play until total asset depletion. Variable-ratio reward schedules maintain play because the next reward could come at any time. The mathematical structure of the game is invisible to the player, who experiences only the surface (lights, sounds, near-misses) while the underlying probability structure ensures net loss over time. The house edge is designed to be imperceptible on a per-spin basis.

findings.quote: Several of the men, like Max Kampelman, agreed that nearly immediately after semistarvation began, all interest in women and dating was lost: "I can tell you, the sex drive disappeared. There was none."
findings.content: The Minnesota Starvation Experiment (Keys, 1944-45, 36 conscientious objectors under controlled semi-starvation) documents reproductive-axis shutdown under sustained energy deficit: sexual interest collapsed almost immediately once semi-starvation began, while food became the dominant preoccupation and social engagement narrowed. Evidence that an unresolved M13 deficit suppresses M14, supporting state-dependent drive priority: DA8 priority relations behave as slope functions of current state rather than a fixed order.
findings.where: Section on the psychological effects of semistarvation, participant interviews

findings.quote: in our Whitehall II study of British civil servants we also found: the lower the rank, the lower the HDL cholesterol. All things considered, we thought better of trying to adopt Sapolsky's darting technique for our civil servants. We did, however, find that the metabolic syndrome increased in frequency as the hierarchy was descended: the lower the employment grade, the lower the HDL cholesterol, the higher the plasma triglyceride, the higher the fasting levels of glucose and insulin. The lower the grade, the higher the waist:hip ratio. It is important to make the distinction between this central pattern of obesity and simple overweight, where the excess body fat is more widely distributed.
findings.content: In Whitehall II, the metabolic syndrome increased in frequency as the civil-service hierarchy was descended: the lower the employment grade, the lower the HDL cholesterol, the higher the plasma triglyceride, the higher the fasting levels of glucose and insulin. The lower the grade, the higher the waist:hip ratio. This central adiposity may be the result of a complex series of reactions involving cortisol metabolism; central obesity occurs in Cushing's Syndrome, a disorder characterised by over-secretion of cortisol.
findings.where: Chapter 4 'Stress in the Jungle? Stress in the Office?' pp. 121-122, citing Whitehall II metabolic markers

findings.quote: A wave of obesity and chronic, preventable illnesses and disabilities is sweeping across the globe. These preventable diseases include certain cancers, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, heart disease, strokes, kidney disease, some allergies, dementia, depression, anxiety, insomnia, and other illnesses.
findings.content: A wave of preventable chronic illnesses is sweeping across the globe: certain cancers, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, heart disease, strokes, kidney disease, allergies, dementia, depression, anxiety, insomnia. Billions also suffer from lower back pain, fallen arches, plantar fasciitis, myopia, arthritis, constipation, and acid reflux. These are mismatch diseases - conditions whose prevalence surged when human environments departed from the conditions under which human bodies evolved.

The Danish 2-week sedentary-forced experiment: healthy young men paid to sit for a fortnight and take no more than 1500 steps per day (about a mile) gained 7% more organ (visceral) fat and began to exhibit classic signs of chronic inflammation including reduced ability to take up blood sugar after a meal. The mechanism is clear: inactivity + adequate calories → organ fat accumulation → inflammatory cytokines → metabolic dysregulation. This is load-bearing for the M10/M8/DC1 cascade - sedentarism drives the allostatic-load pathway through the organ-fat-inflammation channel.

findings.quote: Here we tested a Constrained total energy expenditure model, in which total energy expenditure increases with physical activity at low activity levels but plateaus at higher activity levels as the body adapts to maintain total energy expenditure within a narrow range. We compared total energy expenditure, measured using doubly labeled water, against physical activity, measured using accelerometry, for a large (n = 332) sample of adults living in five populations. After adjusting for body size and composition, total energy expenditure was positively correlated with physical activity, but the relationship was markedly stronger over the lower range of physical activity. For subjects in the upper range of physical activity, total energy expenditure plateaued, supporting a Constrained total energy expenditure model.
findings.content: The constrained total energy expenditure model: total daily energy expenditure (TEE) increases with physical activity at low activity levels but plateaus at higher levels as the body adapts metabolically to maintain TEE within a narrow range. Tested in a multi-population doubly-labeled-water study (n=332 adults from Ghana, Jamaica, Seychelles, South Africa, and the US). Above moderate activity, each additional increment of ~100 counts per minute per day was associated with less than 50 kcal/day increase in TEE. The change point from positive slope to zero was 230 CPM/day. Load-bearing for M13 Energy Regulation: the body is homeostatically buffered against habitual activity variation, and exercise does not produce linear caloric deficits.
findings.where: Pontzer et al. 2016 Current Biology 26:410-417, Abstract / Introduction

findings.quote: People in less socioeconomically developed populations, including subsistence farmers and traditional hunter-gatherers, have total energy expenditures similar to those in more developed populations despite substantial differences in physical activity. Mammals living in the wild, including non-human primate species, have total energy expenditures similar to captive populations. These population-level comparisons suggest that total energy expenditure is an evolved, species-specific trait that is homeostatically buffered against variation in habitual physical activity.
findings.content: Cross-population pattern: people in less socioeconomically developed populations - subsistence farmers and traditional hunter-gatherers - have total energy expenditures similar to those in more developed populations despite substantial differences in physical activity. Non-human mammals in the wild show the same pattern: wild and captive populations have similar TEE. These population-level comparisons suggest that total energy expenditure is an evolved, species-specific trait that is homeostatically buffered against variation in habitual physical activity. This is the foundational empirical pattern that the Constrained TEE model is designed to explain.
findings.where: Pontzer et al. 2016, Introduction / Cross-population synthesis

findings.quote: These illnesses are mismatch diseases, defined as diseases that result from our Paleolithic bodies being poorly or inadequately adapted to certain modern behaviors and conditions. I don't think it is possible to overemphasize just how important mismatch diseases are. You are most likely going to die from a mismatch disease. You are most likely to suffer from disabilities caused by mismatch diseases. Mismatch diseases contribute to the bulk of health-care spending throughout the world.
findings.content: Lieberman's foundational mismatch-disease framework from The Story of the Human Body (2013). Evolutionary medicine identifies 'mismatch diseases' - illnesses caused by our bodies being poorly or inadequately adapted to certain modern behaviors and conditions. The framework analogizes human mismatch to transplanting a zebra to New England: the organism is still well-adapted for its original environment but the new environment is wrong. Over 50% of healthcare spending worldwide goes toward mismatch diseases. This is the architectural framing for P3 Systematic Mismatch at the chronic-disease-epidemiology scale and the theoretical backbone for Lieberman's subsequent Exercised (2021).
findings.where: Lieberman, The Story of the Human Body (2013) Part II opening, pp. ~181

findings.quote: The simplest way to classify mismatch diseases is by how a given environmental stimulus has changed. Broadly speaking, most mismatch diseases occur when a common stimulus either increases or decreases beyond levels for which the body is adapted, or when the stimulus is entirely novel and the body is not adapted for it at all. Put simply, mismatches are caused by stimuli that are too much, too little, or too new. For example, as cultural evolution transforms people's diets, some mismatch diseases occur from eating too much fat, others from eating too little fat, and yet others from eating new kinds of fat that the body cannot digest (such as partially hydrogenated fats).
findings.content: Lieberman's taxonomy of mismatch causes - 'too much, too little, or too new'. Mismatch diseases occur when a common environmental stimulus either increases or decreases beyond levels for which the body is adapted, or when the stimulus is entirely novel and the body is not adapted for it at all. For diet specifically: some mismatch diseases come from eating too much fat, others from eating too little fat, others from eating new kinds of fat the body cannot digest (partially hydrogenated fats). This classification is load-bearing for M13 Energy Regulation - the mechanism handles each of these three categories differently, and the too-much/too-little/too-new framing helps distinguish among specific M13 cascade failures.
findings.where: Lieberman, The Story of the Human Body (2013), Chapter on mismatch classification

findings.quote: According to Jared Diamond, farming was the 'worst mistake in the history of the human race.' In spite of having more food, hence more children, than hunter-gatherers, farmers generally have to work harder; they eat a lower-quality diet; they more often confront starvation because their crops occasionally fail from floods, droughts, and other disasters; and they live at higher population densities, which promote infectious diseases and social stress. Farming may have led to civilization and other types of 'progress,' but it also led to misery and death on a grand scale. Most of the mismatch diseases from which we currently suffer stem from the transition from hunting and gathering to farming.
findings.content: Lieberman on the farming transition as a foundational mismatch event. Drawing on Jared Diamond's provocative characterization of farming as 'the worst mistake in the history of the human race', Lieberman argues that most modern mismatch diseases stem from the transition from hunting-gathering to farming: more food but lower-quality diet, harder work, more frequent starvation from crop failures, higher population densities driving infectious disease and social stress. The architectural implication for M13: the first major mismatch in the human metabolic environment came roughly 11,000 years ago, predating the industrial and dietary transitions that Exercised focuses on. Load-bearing for reading M13 failure modes as stacked across multiple historical transitions rather than as a single industrial-era problem.
findings.where: Lieberman, The Story of the Human Body (2013), Chapter on farming transition

findings.content: The discordance hypothesis: the human genome was shaped under Paleolithic nutritional conditions and has changed negligibly since the advent of agriculture (~10,000 years ago). Modern diseases of civilization - atherosclerosis, hypertension, obesity, diabetes - result from the mismatch between our evolved metabolic physiology and contemporary dietary patterns. The genome expects one nutritional environment and receives a fundamentally different one.

Eaton & Konner analyzed nutritional properties of wild game and uncultivated vegetable foods and evaluated archaeological remains to reconstruct Paleolithic diet composition. Their model was derived from 69 game and wild vegetable items. Humanity has existed as a genus for about 2 million years, with evolutionary history making definitive contributions to current genetic composition partly in response to dietary influences. The resulting evolutionary discordance between ancestral and modern diets is proposed as a major source of chronic disease.

findings.quote: We hypothesize that human daily energy expenditure may be an evolved physiological trait largely independent of cultural differences.
findings.content: Pontzer's evolved-trait hypothesis from the 2012 Hadza paper: human daily energy expenditure may be an evolved physiological trait largely independent of cultural differences. This is the theoretical claim that motivated the broader Constrained TEE research program - TEE is not a passive function of behavior but an actively regulated species-typical homeostatic variable. If correct, it reframes the entire energetic basis of obesity: the difference between Hadza and Western adults is not caloric throughput but caloric composition and timing of intake.
findings.where: Pontzer et al. 2012 PLoS ONE 7(7):e40503, Abstract

findings.quote: When Herman Pontzer and his colleagues measured daily energy expenditures in the Hadza, they were surprised to find that the highly active Hadza spend about the same total number of calories per day as sedentary industrialized people with the same lean body weight. In addition, when Pontzer and colleagues collected energetic data from adults in many countries including the United States, Ghana, Jamaica, and South Africa, they observed that more active people spent only slightly more calories per day than more sedentary people who weighed the same. In addition, individuals who were more physically active didn't have total energy budgets as high as their exertions would predict. How could someone who spent five hundred extra calories a day exercising not have a total energy budget that is five hundred calories higher? The proposed explanation is that people's total energy budgets are constrained: if I use five hundred extra calories walking, I'll spend less energy on my resting metabolism to help pay for my exertions.
findings.content: The Pontzer constrained energy expenditure hypothesis: highly active Hadza spend about the same total daily energy as sedentary industrialized people with the same lean body weight. Across countries (US, Ghana, Jamaica, South Africa), more active people spend only slightly more calories per day than sedentary people of the same weight. The proposed mechanism is metabolic compensation - when one burns extra calories exercising, resting metabolism is reduced to keep total energy budget roughly constant. This is load-bearing for M13 Energy Regulation and for DA4 (exercise-as-weight-loss is a weak proxy for metabolic health).

findings.quote: We hypothesize that non-muscular physiological activity contributes substantially to activity energy expenditure 2 and its adaptation to physical activity. Human studies and non-human animal models show that energy allocation across a broad range of physiological tasks, including reproductive activity and somatic maintenance, may be reduced when physical activity increases, resulting in decreased activity energy expenditure 2. Indeed, such physical activity-induced reduction in activity energy expenditure 2 could potentially contribute to the beneficial health effects of exercise, reducing energy expenditure on inflammation and detrimental immune system activity.
findings.content: Pontzer's non-muscular compensation hypothesis: the component of activity energy expenditure that compensates for increased physical activity is unlikely to be purely muscular. When the analysis limits to subjects above 230 CPM/day, activity energy expenditure 2 (the compensatory component) is too large to be accounted for by reductions in standing, fidgeting, or peripheral limb movement alone. Pontzer hypothesizes that non-muscular physiological activity - reproductive activity, somatic maintenance, inflammation, immune system activity - is reduced when physical activity increases, absorbing the expected caloric deficit. This frames physical activity as a regulator of systemic energy allocation across multiple physiological domains, not merely as direct caloric expenditure.
findings.where: Pontzer et al. 2016, Discussion section on activity energy expenditure components

findings.quote: We get sick from chronic diseases by doing what we evolved to do but under conditions for which our bodies are poorly adapted, and we then pass on those same conditions to our children, who also then get sick.
findings.content: Humans get sick from chronic diseases by doing what they evolved to do but under conditions their bodies are poorly adapted to, then pass those conditions to their children in a vicious cycle. Lieberman calls this dysevolution - an intergenerational feedback loop where mismatch diseases persist because modern environments prevent natural selection from eliminating the underlying susceptibilities.

findings.quote: Humans evolved to be prone to obesity not because excess fat makes us healthy, but because it increases fertility. Along the same lines, our species' proclivities to be worried, anxious, and stressed cause much misery and unhappiness, but they are ancient adaptations to avoid or cope with danger.
findings.content: Humans evolved to be prone to obesity not because excess fat makes us healthy but because it increases fertility. Anxiety, worry, and stress cause misery and unhappiness but they are ancient adaptations to avoid or cope with danger. The mismatch hypothesis - that human bodies were adapted for very different conditions - is the core of evolutionary medicine.

findings.quote: diabetes is a growing problem because human bodies, like those of captive primates, were adapted primarily for very different conditions that render us inadequately adapted to cope with modern diets and physical inactivity.
findings.content: Type 2 diabetes is a mismatch disease: human bodies, like captive primates, were adapted for very different conditions and are inadequately adapted to cope with modern diets and physical inactivity. The answer does not lie solely in cellular and genetic mechanisms but in the evolutionary mismatch between ancestral and modern environments.

The Paleolithic nutrition model identifies specific discordances between ancestral and modern diets: higher protein intake, lower carbohydrate (especially refined), much higher fiber, lower sodium, higher potassium, higher calcium from non-dairy sources, and substantially lower sugar consumption. The fat profile differs in kind, not just quantity - ancestral fats were predominantly unsaturated while modern diets are dominated by saturated and trans fats. These specific nutritional parameters define the mismatch that drives metabolic disease.

findings.quote: My last book, The Story of the Human Body, made the case that many of the diseases that kill us slowly today are mismatch diseases caused by our bodies being imperfectly or inadequately adapted to modern environmental conditions like smoking, obesity, and physical inactivity. Although these diseases are commonly classified as diseases of aging because they tend to arise when we are middle-aged, they are not caused by age, nor should they be considered inevitable consequences of aging. Plenty of people live to old age without getting these diseases, which rarely if ever afflict elderly hunter-gatherers and many aged people who live in subsistence societies.
findings.content: Lieberman's explicit mismatch framing of the epidemiological transition and 'diseases of aging'. Many chronic noninfectious diseases that kill us slowly today (heart disease, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer's, chronic respiratory disease, osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, autoimmune diseases) are mismatch diseases caused by our bodies being inadequately adapted to modern environmental conditions like smoking, obesity, and physical inactivity. Although they are commonly classified as 'diseases of aging' because they tend to arise in middle age, they are not caused by aging per se and are rare among elderly hunter-gatherers. This grounds P3 (systematic mismatch) at the epidemiological scale and M10 specifically as one of the three primary mismatch axes.

findings.quote: Farming brought many advantages but also caused many serious problems. Farming enabled humans to have more food, hence more children, but also required new forms of work, transformed diets, and opened a Pandora's box of diseases and social ills.
findings.content: Farming brought many advantages but also caused serious problems. It enabled more food and hence more children, but also required new forms of work, transformed diets, and opened a Pandora's box of diseases and social ills. The agricultural revolution was the first major dysevolution event - the transition from foraging to farming created the first systematic mismatch between human bodies and their environment.

findings.quote: Human psychological mechanisms are adaptations that evolved to process environmental inputs, turning them into behavioral outputs that, on average, increase survival or reproductive prospects. Modern contexts, however, differ vastly from the environments that existed as human psychological mechanisms evolved.
findings.content: Evolutionary mismatch occurs when human psychological mechanisms, adapted to process ancestral environmental inputs, encounter modern contexts that differ vastly from those environments. Many inputs now differ in quantity, intensity, or no longer have the same fitness associations, leading mechanisms to produce maladaptive output. Li et al. classify mismatch along four dimensions: source (natural vs human-induced), type (forced vs hijacked), cause (input changes vs output-consequence changes), and consequences (effects on reproductive fitness crossed with effects on individual well-being). Tables 1-3 provide worked examples for each dimension.
findings.where: Current Directions in Psychological Science 27(1):38-44, 2018. DOI: 10.1177/0963721417731378

findings.quote: Sexual incentive stimuli activate sexual motivation and heighten the level of general arousal. The sexual motive may induce the individual to approach the incentive, and eventually to initiate sexual acts.
findings.content: The incentive-motivation account of M14: sexual motivation is activated by external sexual incentive stimuli interacting with a central motive state; it is not a homeostatic reservoir in which unexpended sexual energy accumulates as an internal need. The review endorses Beach's rejection of an internal origin ("sexual motivation is active only in the presence of an external stimulus") and builds the modern model on Bindra and Toates incentive theory. No tissue deficit accumulates during abstinence; desire follows cue-triggered arousal rather than spontaneous internal pressure. For activation_class: event_triggered (incentive), not homeostatic.

findings.quote: Thus, in rats and humans there is no doubt that testicular hormones, either directly or via aromatization, are in charge of the control of the long-term activity of the sexual central motive state.
findings.content: Hormones set the gain, not the pressure: in rats and humans, testicular hormones control the long-term activity level of the sexual central motive state (in men via androgen receptors directly; in rats partly via aromatization to estrogens), while short-term variation in sexual motivation is driven by incentive stimuli, not by hormone fluctuation. The same structure is proposed for women (androgens needed for basic long-term activity of the central motive state). This is the hormonal gain-modulation half of M14's activation profile: testosterone tunes cue-sensitivity; cues do the triggering.
findings.where: Section on endocrine control of the central motive state

findings.quote: when my colleagues redid this brain scanning experiment in China, their Chinese participants showed just as much activity in the VTA and other dopamine pathways - the neurochemical pathways for wanting. Almost everyone on earth feels this passion. In fact, because the VTA lies near primitive brain regions associated with thirst and hunger, I came to realize that romantic love is a basic human drive. My brain scanning partner Lucy Brown has added to this perspective, saying that romantic love is a survival mechanism as crucial as the craving for water.
findings.content: When Fisher's colleagues redid the brain scanning experiment in China, their Chinese participants showed just as much activity in the VTA and other dopamine pathways - the neurochemical pathways for wanting. Almost everyone on earth feels this passion. Because the VTA lies near primitive brain regions associated with thirst and hunger, romantic love is a basic human drive. Romantic love is a survival mechanism as crucial as the craving for water.
findings.where: Chapter 2 'The Drive to Love... a Natural Addiction' pp. 34-35, citing Xiaomeng Xu and colleagues' Chinese replication

findings.quote: The Taita of Kenya say that love comes in two forms: an irresistible longing, a 'kind of sickness'; and a deep, enduring affection for another. Brazilians say, 'Love is born in a glance and matures in a smile.' For the Koreans, sarang is a word close to the Western concept of romantic love, while chong is more like feelings of long-term attachment.
findings.content: Love is distinguished by men and women around the world. The Taita of Kenya say that love comes in two forms: an irresistible longing, a 'kind of sickness'; and a deep, enduring affection for another. Brazilians say, 'Love is born in a glance and matures in a smile.' For the Koreans, sarang is a word close to the Western concept of romantic love, while chong is more like feelings of long-term attachment. Nisa, the !Kung woman of the Kalahari Desert, explained the arc of love: 'When two people are first together, their hearts are on fire and their passion is very great. After a while, the fire cools and that's how it stays. They continue to love each other, but it's in a different way - warm and dependable.'

findings.quote: In the early 1970s, it was still widely assumed by Darwinians that females were sexually passive and "coy." Female langurs were anything but. When bands of roving males approached the troop, females would solicit them or actually leave their troop to go in search of them. On occasion, a female mated with invaders even though she was already pregnant and not ovulating (something else nonhuman primates were not supposed to do).
findings.content: Hrdy's central reframing of female sexuality: In the 1970s Darwinians widely assumed females were sexually passive and 'coy'. Female langurs were anything but - they solicited invading males or left their troop to find them, and mated with invaders even while pregnant and not ovulating. Hrdy's interpretation: mothers were insuring paternity uncertainty as an infanticide-avoidance strategy. This overturns the passive-female Darwinian framing and grounds M14 Reproductive Motivation in a specifically female-agency frame rather than a male-pursuit frame.

Study 2 novel prediction: EMT predicts a complementary bias in women - underperception of men's commitment (because the cost of falsely inferring commitment and being abandoned with offspring was historically much greater for women than the cost of missing a real commitment signal). Haselton and Buss documented the commitment underperception effect: women significantly underestimated men's commitment levels relative to men's self-reports, in the same paradigm in which men overestimated women's sexual intent. This was a novel a priori prediction derived directly from the asymmetric cost structure - a stronger test of EMT than the already-known sexual overperception effect.

findings.quote: Men who inherited this gene scored significantly lower on the Partner Bonding Scale, a questionnaire that measures one's degree of attachment to a mate. Moreover, scores were dose-dependent. Men carrying two copies of this gene showed the lowest scores on the Partner Bonding Scale; those carrying one copy expressed more feelings of attachment; and men who had no copies of this gene were the most attached to their partner. Men carrying this vasopressin gene had also experienced more marital crises during the previous year, including threats of divorce. Once again, these results were dose-dependent. Last, the spouses of men with one or two copies of this gene scored significantly lower on questionnaires measuring marital satisfaction.
findings.content: A Swedish study of 552 men, all either married or living with a partner for at least five years, investigated whether a vasopressin-receptor gene affects pair-bonding behavior. Men who inherited this gene scored significantly lower on the Partner Bonding Scale. Scores were dose-dependent: men carrying two copies of this gene showed the lowest scores; those carrying one copy expressed more feelings of attachment; and men who had no copies of this gene were the most attached to their partner. Men carrying this vasopressin gene had also experienced more marital crises during the previous year, including threats of divorce. Spouses of men with one or two copies of this gene scored significantly lower on questionnaires measuring marital satisfaction.
findings.where: Chapter 4 'Why Adultery?' pp. 93-94, Walum et al. 2008 AVPR1A finding

findings.quote: And men feel this passion just as powerfully as women. Tennov wrote of her 800+ informants that men and women experienced this intense passion 'in roughly equal proportions.' My colleagues and I have now confirmed this. In our fMRI study of young happy lovers, men showed just as much activity in the VTA and other neural pathways for romantic passion as women did.
findings.content: In our fMRI studies of romantic love, men and women showed equivalent activation in the core romantic-love brain regions (VTA and related dopamine pathways). Tennov reported that men and women experience this passion in roughly equal proportions from her 800+ informants. In contrast to folk belief that men are less emotional or less capable of romantic love, the neural data show men and women feel this passion equivalently.

findings.quote: When a female prairie vole begins to express attraction to a male vole, she experiences a 50% increase of dopamine activity in parts of this reward system. An increase of dopamine in the brain is also associated with mate attraction in female sheep. Hence, this neural mechanism for attraction must have evolved in many species of birds and mammals - to enable individuals to prefer and focus on specific mating partners, thereby conserving valuable courtship time and energy.
findings.content: Cross-species evidence: when a female prairie vole begins to express attraction to a male vole, she experiences a 50% increase of dopamine activity in parts of the reward system. An increase of dopamine in the brain is also associated with mate attraction in female sheep. This neural mechanism for attraction must have evolved in many species of birds and mammals - to enable individuals to prefer and focus on specific mating partners, thereby conserving valuable courtship time and energy.
findings.where: Chapter 2 'The Drive to Love... a Natural Addiction' p. 36

findings.quote: when neuroscientist Larry Young and colleagues modified a harmless virus to carry the genetic code for vasopressin receptors and injected the virus into males of another species, meadow voles (creatures that do not form pair-bonds), these animals also began to make solid attachments to their current sexual partners. And most important to this book: men with related genes for vasopressin transmission also tend to make more stable partnerships.
findings.content: Larry Young and colleagues modified a harmless virus to carry the genetic code for vasopressin receptors and injected the virus into males of meadow voles - creatures that do not normally form pair-bonds. These animals then began to make solid attachments to their current sexual partners. This direct genetic manipulation from non-monogamous to monogamous behavior at the single-gene level is one of the strongest demonstrations that the vasopressin system is causally involved in mammalian pair-bonding.
findings.where: Chapter 7 'Satisfaction Hormones' pp. 178-179, citing Larry Young prairie vole → meadow vole vector experiment

findings.quote: We are a pair-bonding species. Some 85% of cultures permit a man to have several wives, but few men actually build a harem. A man has to have a lot of goats, cows, land, money, or other impressive resources to get several women to share his wedding bed. Even then, having more than one wife can be a toothache. Co-wives fight; sometimes they even poison one another's children. We are built to rear our babies as a team of two - with a lot of helpers near the nest.
findings.content: Fisher's cross-cultural / cross-species framing of human reproductive architecture. The pair-bonding species claim is grounded in two distinct empirical observations from different parts of the book: (a) the cross-cultural pattern - 85% of cultures permit polygyny but most men have only one wife at a time (Fisher prologue, source lines 100-106); and (b) the cross-species rarity - only 3% of mammals form pair-bonds to rear their young, while ~90% of avian species do (Fisher Chapter 3 on adultery in other species, source line 1710). The two findings jointly establish pair-bonding as part of human architecture while showing it is a robust but distinctive mammalian pattern.
findings.where: Prologue and Chapter 3 'Is Monogamy Natural?' pp. 1 and 39-40

findings.content: Hrdy's identification of infanticide as widespread across primate taxa: infanticide by males is documented across many primate species, establishing it as a recurrent evolutionary pressure shaping female reproductive strategy across primates broadly, not a pathological anomaly of a few species. This cross-taxon distribution is load-bearing for P1 Inclusive Fitness and for M14 Reproductive Motivation's architectural shaping by infanticide risk.

findings.quote: Please recall the prairie vole. These individuals form lifelong pair-bonds soon after puberty and raise several litters as a team. And this pairing has been directly correlated with neurochemical activities in the brain. When prairie voles first engage in sex, copulation triggers activity in oxytocin receptors (in the nucleus accumbens) among females and vasopressin receptors (in the ventral pallidum) among males. This stimulates dopamine release in several brain regions - producing feelings of wanting, seeking, focus, energy, pleasure, and motivation - driving these furry little creatures to prefer a particular mate, initiate a pair-bond, and express enduring attachment behaviors. But specific variations in a particular gene in the vasopressin system contribute to variability in the strength of a male prairie vole's pair-bond, including the degree to which a male expresses sexual fidelity to his partner.
findings.content: When prairie voles first engage in sex, copulation triggers activity in oxytocin receptors (in the nucleus accumbens) among females and vasopressin receptors (in the ventral pallidum) among males. This stimulates dopamine release in several brain regions - producing feelings of wanting, seeking, focus, energy, pleasure, and motivation - driving these furry little creatures to prefer a particular mate, initiate a pair-bond, and express enduring attachment behaviors. Specific variations in a particular gene in the vasopressin system contribute to variability in the strength of a male prairie vole's pair-bond, including the degree to which a male expresses sexual fidelity to his partner.
findings.where: Chapter 4 'Why Adultery?' Biology of Adultery section, pp. 92-93

findings.quote: This article explores the possibility that romantic love is an attachment process--a biosocial process by which affectional bonds are formed between adult lovers, just as affectional bonds are formed earlier in life between human infants and their parents.
findings.content: Adult romantic love is an attachment process: affectional bonds form between adult lovers just as between infants and parents. Three adult attachment styles parallel Ainsworth's infant categories. Distribution: ~56% secure, ~25% avoidant, ~19% anxious-ambivalent (N=620 in Study 1), closely matching infant distributions (~62/23/15%). Secure adults describe relationships as happy, friendly, trusting. Avoidant adults fear closeness and doubt romantic love exists. Anxious adults experience love as obsessive with constant abandonment worry.

findings.quote: Sleep deprived people are perceived as less attractive, less healthy, and more tired compared with when they are well rested.
findings.content: Sleep deprivation is visible in the phenotype: independent judges rate sleep-deprived individuals as less healthy, less attractive, and more fatigued than well-rested individuals from photographs alone. On Cor's reading (not something the study tested, since it measured only perceived health and attractiveness), this makes sleep a phenotypic fitness signal: the physiological state produced by adequate sleep is visible to potential mates and social partners, and sleep loss degrades that signal.

findings.quote: Our findings suggest that T mediates tradeoffs between mating and parenting in humans, as seen in other species in which fathers care for young.
findings.content: Longitudinal study of 624 Filipino men followed 4.5 years (Cebu cohort). Single nonfathers with high waking testosterone at baseline were more likely to become partnered fathers by follow-up. Men who became partnered fathers then showed large declines in waking (median -26%) and evening (median -34%) testosterone, significantly exceeding the declines of men who stayed single nonfathers. Fathers reporting 3 or more hours of daily childcare had lower testosterone at follow-up than fathers not involved in care. Testosterone and reproductive strategy are bidirectional in human males: high testosterone predicts mating success, then testosterone drops when men take up direct care of offspring.
findings.where: PNAS 108(39):16194-16199. Abstract + Results, full text via PMC3182719.

findings.quote: Then, with neuroscientist Lucy Brown, psychologist Art Aron, and others, I put seventeen new lovers into the brain scanner: ten women and seven men who had been madly and happily in love for an average of 7.4 months. I will never forget the moment I first saw the results. I was standing in a darkened lab at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine. I felt like jumping in the sky. Before my eyes were scans showing blobs of activity in the ventral tegmental area, or VTA, a tiny factory near the base of the brain that makes dopamine and sends this natural stimulant to many brain regions. We found activity in many other brain regions, but the VTA was particularly important. This factory is part of the brain's reward system, the brain network that generates wanting, seeking, craving, energy, focus, and motivation.
findings.content: Fisher and colleagues put seventeen new lovers into the fMRI scanner - ten women and seven men who had been madly and happily in love for an average of 7.4 months. The scans showed blobs of activity in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), a tiny factory near the base of the brain that makes dopamine and sends this natural stimulant to many brain regions. This factory is part of the brain's reward system, the brain network that generates wanting, seeking, craving, energy, focus, and motivation. The VTA was particularly important. Men showed just as much activity in the VTA and other neural pathways for romantic passion as women did.
findings.where: Chapter 2 'Why Him? Why Her?' Romantic Attraction fMRI study, pp. 33-34, with Lucy Brown, Art Aron, and colleagues

findings.quote: This drive, this survival mechanism, is also an addiction. With a reanalysis of the data, we found activity in the nucleus accumbens (unpublished data), a brain region that is part of the reward system, is fueled by dopamine, and is associated with all of the addictions - including the cravings for heroin, cocaine, nicotine, alcohol, amphetamines, gambling, sex, and food.
findings.content: With a reanalysis of the Fisher/Brown/Aron fMRI data, activity was found in the nucleus accumbens - a brain region that is part of the reward system, is fueled by dopamine, and is associated with all of the addictions - including the cravings for heroin, cocaine, nicotine, alcohol, amphetamines, gambling, sex, and food. Romantic love is, in this architectural sense, a natural addiction, running through the same reward pathways that pathological addictions hijack.
findings.where: Chapter 2 'The Drive to Love... a Natural Addiction' pp. 35

findings.quote: in another of our brain scanning experiments, led this time by psychologist Bianca Acevedo, we put seventeen long-married women and men into the fMRI scanner, ten women and seven men. Their average length of marriage was twenty-one years; most had grown children; and all had told us that they were still in love with their spouse. The results were astonishing: the VTA and other basic brain regions associated with early-stage intense romantic love were just as active among these long-term lovers as among our newly-in-love younger men and women. With one exception: Our newly-in-love participants showed activity in a specific brain region associated with anxiety, whereas in our long-term lovers this angst was replaced by new activity in brain regions linked with calm and pain suppression.
findings.content: In Acevedo et al.'s fMRI brain scanning experiment, seventeen long-married women and men were scanned while viewing photos of their spouse. Average length of marriage was twenty-one years; most had grown children; all said they were still in love with their spouse. The results were astonishing: the VTA and other basic brain regions associated with early-stage intense romantic love were just as active among these long-term lovers as among newly-in-love younger men and women. One exception: newly-in-love participants showed activity in a brain region associated with anxiety, whereas in long-term lovers this angst was replaced by new activity in brain regions linked with calm and pain suppression.
findings.where: Chapter 2 'The Trajectory of Love' pp. 38-39, Acevedo, Aron, Fisher, Brown long-term marriage fMRI study

findings.quote: Several of the men, like Max Kampelman, agreed that nearly immediately after semistarvation began, all interest in women and dating was lost: "I can tell you, the sex drive disappeared. There was none."
findings.content: The Minnesota Starvation Experiment (Keys, 1944-45, 36 conscientious objectors under controlled semi-starvation) documents reproductive-axis shutdown under sustained energy deficit: sexual interest collapsed almost immediately once semi-starvation began, while food became the dominant preoccupation and social engagement narrowed. Evidence that an unresolved M13 deficit suppresses M14, supporting state-dependent drive priority: DA8 priority relations behave as slope functions of current state rather than a fixed order.
findings.where: Section on the psychological effects of semistarvation, participant interviews

findings.quote: oxytocin, which mediates various pro-social processes, including maternal behavior and the inhibition of separation distress (Chapters 12 to 14), can yield a tripeptide called PLG (proline-leucine-glycine), which mediates none of the above but has antidepressant effects.
findings.content: Panksepp's early summary of oxytocin's pro-social functions: oxytocin mediates various pro-social processes including female sexual response, orgasm, maternal behavior, social memory, and the INHIBITION of separation distress. It is a single neuropeptide that operates across the sexual-maternal-social-bonding domains - exactly the molecular overlap that allows evolution to construct the 'social contract' by repurposing reproductive circuits for broader bonding. This is primary-source evidence for the M14/M9/M3 architectural overlap in Cor's specification.

findings.quote: A large body of observational data from the Wisconsin laboratories indicates that heterosexual behaviour is greatly influenced by early experience, and the failure of infants to form effective infant-infant affectional relations delays or destroys adequate adult heterosexual behaviour
findings.content: Harlow's deprivation experiments with rhesus monkeys: infants reared in social environments differing greatly from the environment of evolutionary adaptedness show severe disruption. Failure to form effective infant-infant affectional relations delays or destroys adequate adult heterosexual behavior. Even monkeys with adequate peer play but no maternal experience show considerable individual differences in adult social and sexual competence.

findings.quote: Brain activations occurred in several regions of the reward system. Included were regions of the ventral tegmental area (VTA) associated with feelings of intense romantic love; the ventral pallidum, associated with feelings of deep attachment; the insular cortex and the anterior cingulate, associated with physical pain, anxiety, and the distress associated with physical pain; and the nucleus accumbens and orbitofrontal/prefrontal cortex, brain regions associated with assessing one's gains and losses - as well as craving and addiction. Most relevant to our story, activity in several of these brain regions has been correlated with the craving for cocaine and other drugs.
findings.content: When my colleagues redid the brain scanning experiment to look at rejection, we found that feelings of romantic rejection lit up activity in several brain regions linked with profound attachment, deep addiction, and physical pain. When you are rejected in love, many brain systems go to work, and rejection is one of the most painful experiences a human being can endure.
findings.where: Chapter 5 'Blueprint for Divorce' pp. 127-128, Fisher/Brown rejection fMRI study

findings.quote: the ancient subcortical regions of mammalian brains contain at least seven emotional, or affective, systems: SEEKING (expectancy), FEAR (anxiety), RAGE (anger), LUST (sexual excitement), CARE (nurturance), PANIC/GRIEF (sadness), and PLAY (social joy). Each of these systems controls distinct but specific types of behaviors associated with many overlapping physiological changes.
findings.content: The ancient subcortical regions of mammalian brains contain at least seven emotional systems: SEEKING (expectancy), FEAR (anxiety), RAGE (anger), LUST (sexual excitement), CARE (nurturance), PANIC/GRIEF (sadness), and PLAY (social joy). Each controls distinct behaviors with overlapping physiological changes and generates distinct types of affective consciousness. When stimulated in humans, people always experience intense emotional feelings. Capitalizations indicate that real physical and distinct networks for these emotions exist in mammalian brains.

findings.quote: primal emotional systems are made up of neuroanatomies and neurochemistries that are remarkably similar across all mammalian species. This suggests that these systems evolved a very long time ago and that at a basic emotional and motivational level, all mammals are more similar than they are different.
findings.content: Primal emotional systems are made up of neuroanatomies and neurochemistries remarkably similar across all mammalian species. This suggests these systems evolved a very long time ago and that at a basic emotional and motivational level, all mammals are more similar than different. Deep in the ancient affective recesses of our brains, we remain evolutionarily kin. The same neural paths and brain chemicals that arouse each of these seven systems are found within all mammals.

Panksepp's textbook Affective Neuroscience establishes the methodology and evidence base for the seven subcortical affective systems. Across cross-species deep brain stimulation, lesion, and pharmacological studies, the same brain regions produce the same functional categories of affective response - SEEKING, FEAR, RAGE, LUST, CARE, PANIC, PLAY - across mammals, providing the empirical foundation for treating these as conserved motivational architecture rather than culturally constructed categories.

findings.quote: FEAR is an inborn capacity of the mammalian brain. However, FEAR, just like all other basic emotions, rapidly gets enmeshed with world events as it comes to be regulated by learning and encoded in our conscious minds.
findings.content: FEAR is an inborn capacity of the mammalian brain that rapidly gets enmeshed with world events through learning. Most basic emotions need not be expressed immediately after birth. Some - including CARE, LUST, and PLAY - come online long after others such as SEEKING, RAGE, and FEAR. The developmental timing reflects phylogenetic priority: the oldest and most survival-critical systems activate earliest.

findings.quote: It has become increasingly clear during the past half century that primary-process affective mechanisms are concentrated in ancient subcortical midline brain regions that are anatomically and neurochemically, and hence, evolutionarily, similar in all mammalian species.
findings.content: Seven distinct emotional systems identified with specific neuroanatomy and neurochemistry: SEEKING (VTA/NAcc/lateral hypothalamus, DA+), RAGE (medial amygdala→BNST→hypothalamus→PAG, substance P+), FEAR (central amygdala→hypothalamus→dorsal PAG, glutamate+/CRF+), LUST (cortico-medial amygdala/BNST/preoptic, steroids+), CARE (anterior cingulate/BNST/preoptic/VTA, oxytocin+/prolactin+), PANIC (anterior cingulate/BNST/dorsomedial thalamus/PAG, opioids−/oxytocin−/CRF+), PLAY (dorsomedial diencephalon/parafascicular/PAG, opioids+/−). Each mapped in Fig. 2 with specific neurochemical modulators.
findings.where: Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 35(9):1791-1804, p. 1795, Fig. 2. DOI: 10.1016/j.neubiorev.2011.08.003

findings.quote: women's mate preferences vary across the reproductive cycle in very specific and theoretically consistent ways
findings.content: According to the strategic pluralism model of mating, women evolved to make trade-offs between two sets of attributes when evaluating men as potential mates: men's degree of health/viability ('good genes') and their level of commitment/investment in the relationship and subsequent offspring. The ovulatory shift hypothesis predicts and confirms that women's mate preferences vary across the reproductive cycle in very specific and theoretically consistent ways - including preference for more symmetrical men as short-term mates specifically during high-fertility windows.
findings.where: Chapter 3, 'Methods of Evolutionary Sciences,' Mate Preferences Across the Reproductive Cycle section, pp. 130-131

findings.quote: In the now classic 'sweaty T-shirt' experiment, women sniffed the T-shirts of several anonymous men and selected the T-shirts of those they felt were the sexiest. Interestingly, they selected the T-shirts of men with genes that were different from their own in a specific region of the immune system, the major histocompatibility complex. Perhaps these women were unconsciously attracted to men with different genes because similarity between partners in this part of the immune system can lead to complications of fertility and pregnancy. Tellingly, in a subsequent investigation, women married to men who shared similar genes in this part of the immune system were also more adulterous. And the more of these genes a woman shared with her spouse, the more extra partners she engaged.
findings.content: In the 'sweaty T-shirt' experiment, women sniffed the T-shirts of anonymous men and selected the T-shirts of those they felt were the sexiest. They selected the T-shirts of men with genes that were different from their own in a specific region of the immune system - the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). These women were unconsciously attracted to men with different MHC genes because similarity between partners in this part of the immune system can lead to complications of fertility and pregnancy.
